The icon is a small soft-green circle with a dark check, above each feature's bold title and description (Powerful Suction | HEPA Filter / Energy-Efficient | User-Friendly Controls). Thin horizontal dividers separate the intro, features and closing paragraph. Don't (relative to p.124): one long single-column feature list.
auditCheck: Is a list of ≥4 (inference) short, equally structured features/benefits laid out in a single tall column with a lot of unused horizontal space? Could it be a 2-column grid?
restyleFix: Use `grid grid-cols-2 gap-*` for short feature items (icon above title above 1-2 line description). Add subtle divider lines between content groups.

title: Go beyond the given content: add extra content types (colour-coded icons, comparison visual)
rule: Don't let given product descriptions or stakeholder guidelines cap the design. Use them as a starting point and look for other angles or content types that add value to the product page. The example adds: (a) distinct tinted icons per feature (instead of identical checks), and (b) a comparison bar block: a trophy icon with "3X more powerful suction compare to other brands", and two horizontal bars. The long orange bar is "UltraClean Vacuum Cleaner" and the short pale bar is "Other brands".
why: Aiming for exceptional rather than merely good: extra content that supports the product's claims adds value.
doDont: Do: feature icons are individual and colour-coded in light tinted circles, and the comparison bar sits between dividers above the closing paragraph. Don't: just reproduce the supplied copy as-is.
auditCheck: Does the page only restate the supplied copy? Are the key selling claims (e.g. "3X more powerful") backed by a visual comparison? Are feature icons all identical or generic?
restyleFix: Add a simple bar comparison for the main quantitative claim, with a labelled bar for your product (strong, long, saturated) vs. others (short, pale). Give each feature a meaningful icon in a tinted circle.

title: Look beyond the brief for extra persuasive content
rule: Don't stop at what the brief lists. Ask whether additional benefits or features missing from the brief could tip the scales; whether customer testimonials could add social proof and trust; whether a side-by-side comparison against competitors would help. When you find such opportunities, propose them to key stakeholders even if they are out of the original scope.
why: They deepen user engagement and give the product a competitive edge. Never settle for "good enough" when "even better" is possible. Looking at user needs from different angles improves the whole UX, not just the UI.
doDont: Text only (no visual). Do: propose testimonials, comparison tables and extra benefits. Don't: implement only the literal brief.
auditCheck: Does a landing, pricing or product page that asks for a decision lack social proof (testimonials, ratings, logos) or any comparison against alternatives?
restyleFix: Add a testimonial block and/or a comparison section (us vs competitors) and surface unlisted benefits near the decision point. Flag these as proposals for stakeholders.

title: Be creative but keep every element relevant
rule: Include only information that users or visitors will find useful or informative. For every piece of content ask: "Does this directly benefit the user? Does it answer a question, solve a problem, or improve their understanding of the product or service?" If not, cut it or rephrase it so it is more useful.
why: Irrelevant details clutter the page, detract from the UX and decrease conversion.
doDont: Text only. Do: keep focused, relevant content. Don't: include as much information as possible.
auditCheck: For each block, copy line or decorative widget on the page, can you name the user question it answers? Flag blocks with no answer.
restyleFix: Remove or shorten content that doesn't serve a user need. Rewrite the kept content to be benefit-led.

title: Remove unrelated ads and promos from task flows
rule: The main goal of most interfaces is task completion (sign up, purchase, find info). Any element that doesn't contribute to that goal is a distraction. Don't put unrelated promotional content, such as a "Book a ride to test our new Ferrari – only from $300 per day – Book now" ad with a red CTA button, next to a sign-up form.
why: Distractions increase the risk of errors, abandonment, or a frustrating experience.
doDont: Bad (thumbs-down, from visual): a split-screen sign-up card. The left half has "Create an account for free", email, username and password fields, a terms checkbox and a pale blue "Sign up" button. The right half is a dark Ferrari photo with the heading "Book a ride to test our new Ferrari", the price line and a bright red "Book now" button. The red CTA competes with the blue sign-up button.
auditCheck: Does a sign-up, login or checkout screen contain a second CTA, ad, upsell or promo unrelated to completing that form? Count the competing CTAs on the screen. There should be exactly one primary action.
restyleFix: Delete the promo and its CTA from the flow, or replace it with a non-interactive brand image (see H-04).

title: Use action-free imagery beside forms
rule: A graphic next to a form can help if it supports the brand, evokes the right feeling and improves the aesthetics, as long as it is action-free, with no text and no CTA. It then complements the task instead of competing with it.
why: Balances branding and usability, so it helps task completion without diverting focus.
doDont: Good (thumbs-up, from visual): the same split sign-up card. The right half is a full-bleed photo of a silver sports car on a track under a blue sky, with no text or button. The form sits on a white left half with the pale blue Sign up button as the only CTA. Don't: overlay copy, prices or buttons on the side image (compare H-03).
auditCheck: Does the decorative image next to a form contain any text, button or link? Does it relate to the brand or context?
restyleFix: Replace promotional side panels with a brand-relevant photo or illustration that has no copy or CTAs.

title: Don't stretch forms and CTAs to fill wide screens
rule: On large displays (e.g. MacBook Pro, desktop monitors 1440px wide or more), don't stretch a sign-up form or checkout flow to fill the screen. Don't make inputs and CTAs span almost the full width.
why: Over-stretched fields overwhelm users and make the interface look cluttered. Long lines of text or fields are hard to read and reduce comprehension.
doDont: Bad (thumbs-down, from visual): "Carbana" page with top nav (logo, Home, About, Pricing, Blog, Contact, Sign up button). The form headline, email, username and password inputs, terms checkbox and the pale blue Sign up button all run edge to edge across nearly the whole 1440-wide page, directly on a flat light-grey background with no container.
auditCheck: Is a form input or button wider than roughly a single comfortable column? In code, look for `width:100%` inputs or buttons with no `max-width` on a desktop viewport of 1440px or more, or form fields spanning most of the viewport. (The PDF gives no px max; in the good example in H-06 the card is about 46% of the mockup frame width, from visual – measured on the rendered page image, not a design-px value.)
restyleFix: Put the form in a narrow centered column or card (add `max-width` and `margin: auto`), and let inputs and buttons fill that container only.

title: Contain forms in a defined card and treat white space as a design element
rule: Give input fields and buttons only the space they need. Concentrate the sign-up or checkout fields in a clearly defined box with ample white space around it. Optionally use a different background colour or a subtle image for the surrounding area.
why: Cleaner, more focused experience. White space isn't "wasted": it separates sections and draws attention to what matters most. "White space is your friend."
doDont: Good (thumbs-up, from visual): same Carbana page, but the form sits in a narrow centered white rounded card with a soft shadow, on the light-grey page background. The card is about 46% of the mockup frame width (from visual, measured on the render – not a design-px value), with large empty margins on both sides. Inputs have a grey fill and the Sign up button is full width within the card only.
auditCheck: Is the primary form or checkout content inside a bounded container (card with background, radius or shadow) distinct from the page background? Is the horizontal margin around it generous?
restyleFix: Wrap the form in a card (white fill, radius, soft shadow) centered on a tinted background or subtle image, and leave generous side whitespace.

title: Use overlapping images for depth, but not with clashing edges
rule: Overlapping images or elements can break linear monotony and make the interface feel dynamic, engaging and more sophisticated, but only when done correctly. Plain stacked sections feel segmented. Overlap with no separation between the layers looks jarring.
why: Standard stacked layouts can't match the sophistication of well-done overlap. If the colours of overlapping images clash, the result is visually jarring.
doDont: Example product card "VERSACE EROS" (description, avatar stack, "4.8 (12.6k reviews)" rating with a star). Example 1 (bad / "basic", thumbs-down): a teal water banner image on top. A white content area follows, with a circular product photo (perfume bottle) placed fully below the banner, separated by space. It is functional but segmented and uninspiring. Example 2 (bad, thumbs-down): the circular product photo overlaps the bottom edge of the banner, with no outline. The dark bottle photo and the teal water blend and clash with each other.
auditCheck: Are card layers (banner, avatar or product image) stacked completely apart with no layering, so the card feels flat? Where overlaps exist, is there a visible separating outline or gap between the layers?
restyleFix: Pull the product or avatar image up so it straddles the banner's bottom edge (negative margin/translate), and apply the outline fix in H-08.

title: Give overlapping images an outline that matches the background
rule: When images overlap, give the overlapping image an outline (border) in the same colour as the surface behind it (here white, the card background).
why: This small tweak visually separates each element, creating natural white space and making the overlap work harmoniously.
doDont: Good (thumbs-up, from visual): the VERSACE EROS card where the circular perfume photo straddles the banner's bottom edge and has a thin white ring around it. The avatar stack has white rings too. Don't: leave the overlapping image borderless against the busy banner (see H-07).
auditCheck: For avatars, product thumbnails or circles overlapping another image, is there a border or ring matching the card or background colour (e.g. `border: 2-4px solid <card-bg>`, `ring-white`)? The PDF gives no px value; the ring looks about 2-3px (from visual).
restyleFix: Add a border or ring equal to the background surface colour to every overlapping image, including avatar stacks.

title: Place primary actions in the thumb zone
rule: Mobile devices are often used one-handed, mainly with the thumb. Place key elements (buttons, navigation links, CTAs) and the most-used features within the area the thumb reaches easily. Elements outside it are harder to reach and cause frustration or misclicks.
why: Better usability and a more user-friendly interface on mobile.
doDont: The thumb-zone map (from visual) on a phone: green "Easy to reach" is a blob in the lower-left/lower-middle of the screen. Orange "Stretch but okay" is the middle band and the area right of the green. Red "Hard to reach" is the top of the screen (including the top-left and the top corners) and the bottom-right corner. This map assumes a right-handed thumb (from visual).
auditCheck: On mobile layouts, are the primary CTA, primary navigation and most-used controls in the top third or the far corners? Is the key action reachable in the lower-middle area?
restyleFix: Move primary actions to the bottom of the screen (bottom bar, bottom-anchored CTA) and keep rarely used controls at the top.

title: Anchor onboarding CTAs low on the screen, within thumb reach
rule: Place the main CTA (and the secondary action) near the bottom of the screen where the thumb rests, not at the top. A CTA outside the thumb zone forces users to stretch or adjust their grip.
why: Inconvenient and frustrating, especially for users on the go or with limited mobility. A CTA placed in the thumb zone can be used quickly and easily with one hand.
doDont: Bad (thumbs-down, from visual): a real-estate welcome screen (house photo, headline "Your perfect home is just a search away!", subtext "Explore a wide array of properties right at your fingertips."). The outlined "Sign In" pill sits at the top-right of the screen, far from the thumb. Dark "Sign up" is at the bottom. Good (thumbs-up, from visual): the same screen with both buttons stacked at the bottom, full width and pill-shaped. The outlined "Sign In" is directly above the dark filled "Sign up" below the text. The image and text move upward.
auditCheck: Is any frequently used button (login, sign in, primary CTA) in the top corner of a mobile screen? Are the primary and secondary actions stacked together in the lower part?
restyleFix: Move top-corner auth buttons into a full-width stacked group at the bottom of the screen, with the primary (filled) below or at the very bottom.

title: Don't leave empty states bare
rule: An empty state must not be a blank screen with a bare message such as "You have no projects!". It must offer value and direction.
why: A bare empty state is a dead end. Users feel lost, frustrated, stuck and unsure what to do next, and it wastes an opportunity to guide and engage them.
doDont: Bad (thumbs-down, from visual): a mobile "Projects" screen (back arrow, title, settings gear) with just "You have no projects!" centered in the middle of a blank white card.
auditCheck: Does any list, table, dashboard or inbox render only plain text, or nothing, when it has zero items? Does it lack a CTA?
restyleFix: Replace with a designed empty state (see H-12).

title: Build empty states from illustration, benefit headline, tips and a CTA
rule: A good empty state educates, engages and encourages action. It consists of: (1) a solution-oriented headline ("Start managing your projects and stay organised."), (2) an accompanying illustration to make it visually appealing and less daunting, (3) actionable tips ("Invite team members to collaborate on a project for better communication", "Set deadlines for tasks to keep everyone on track"), and (4) a direct CTA button ("Create new project").
why: It turns a potentially negative experience into a positive one, and the tips and CTA give clear next steps.
doDont: Good (thumbs-up, from visual): a "Projects" screen with a pink-tinted circular illustration (hourglass, calendar, clock, clipboard, lightbulb) at the top. Below it are a bold left-aligned headline, two short tips with small orange lightning-bolt icons in grey text, and a full-width pink pill "Create new project" button at the bottom of the card. Don't: show the bare text in H-11.
auditCheck: Does the empty state include all four parts: headline stating the benefit or next step, a visual, 1-3 tips (inference), and a primary CTA that creates the first item?
restyleFix: Add an illustration, rewrite the headline as an invitation, add 2 short tips with icons, and add a primary CTA button that performs the first action.

title: Error states must explain, offer a fix and match the app's style
rule: A good error state (form validation error, 404 page and so on) must: 1. clearly communicate what went wrong; 2. offer a clear, actionable solution to fix the problem; 3. maintain a consistent visual style with the rest of the application or website.
why: Error states are where journeys often go awry. A bad one leaves users frustrated and confused, not knowing what went wrong or how to fix it. A good one prevents frustration and guides users back on track.
doDont: Bad (thumbs-down, from visual): the Google 404 page shows "404. That's an error. The requested URL /doesnotexist was not found on this server. That's all we know." with a line-art robot illustration. It has no links, no suggestion and no search or action.
auditCheck: Does each error message state the cause in plain language, give a next step (retry, link, field fix), and use the app's regular typography, colours and components? A dead-end message such as "That's all we know" fails.
restyleFix: Rewrite the error copy as cause plus solution, add a primary link or button, and restyle it with the product's own components.

title: Offer helpful links or suggestions on 404 pages
rule: A good 404 page doesn't only say the page can't be found. It also provides helpful links or suggestions that lead the user back on track.
why: It converts a negative experience into a positive one and shows you thought about the user's needs even in the error case. A bare "not found" leaves users lost and frustrated.
doDont: Good (thumbs-up, from visual): Airbnb 404 with the normal site header (logo, "Where to?" search, Become a Host, Sign Up, Log In) kept. A huge "Oops!" heading, "We can't seem to find the page you're looking for.", "Error code: 404", and "Here are some helpful links instead:" followed by a list of coral/red links (Home, Search, Help, Traveling on Airbnb, Hosting on Airbnb, Trust & Safety). A flat illustration of a sad girl with a spilled item sits on the right.
auditCheck: Does the 404 page show the global navigation and provide at least one link, search or suggestion list in addition to the message?
restyleFix: Keep the global header, add 4-6 relevant links or a search box, and show the error code in small text.

title: Express brand personality in error pages
rule: Use the error state as a chance for creativity that reflects the brand's personality: on-brand illustrations, humorous copy or interactive elements that surprise and delight, while still guiding users back to the content they wanted.
why: It makes the error memorable and engaging and leaves a lasting impression, turning a frustrating moment into a positive interaction with the brand.
doDont: Good (thumbs-up, from visual): Disney 404 with the brand header (nav: Disney+, Parks & Travel, Movies, Shop, More, plus search box). A giant "404" has a Disney character (Wreck-It Ralph) in the "0". The humorous line is "You didn't break the internet, but we can't find what you are looking for." A search prompt ("What can KnowsMore help you find today?") with a search field and a mascot character. Don't: use a generic grey system error page (see H-13).
auditCheck: Is the error or 404 page generic (default server style) rather than using brand illustrations, voice or tone? Does it still include a path back (search or links)?
restyleFix: Add an on-brand illustration, a light-hearted line in the brand voice, and keep a search field or links to guide users back.

title: Add icons to navigation dropdown items
rule: Include small icons in top-navigation dropdown items. Icons are visual aids that quickly communicate the purpose or content of a menu item, making the dropdown more attractive and more usable.
why: Improves usability and appeal. Dropdowns help users reach different pages or features intuitively.
doDont: Bad (thumbs-down, from visual): a mega-menu dropdown (two columns: Interactive reports, Team dashboard, Limitless segmentation, Group analytics; Convert, Engage, Retain, Grow). Each item has a bold title and grey description, with no icons and no group headings. The list looks like a flat wall of text. Good (thumbs-up, from visual): the same items, each with a small purple line icon in a light-tinted circle to the left of title and description. The "Group analytics" item carries a green "New" badge.
auditCheck: Are dropdown or mega-menu items text-only, with no leading icon or visual marker? Are icon styles consistent (same stroke, same size, same tint)?
restyleFix: Add a consistent set of line icons (in a light-tinted circle container, from visual) to the left of each item title.

title: Group related dropdown items under category headings
rule: Group related items in a dropdown under distinct categories, so users quickly grasp the navigation structure and find what they need.
why: Helps users understand structure quickly.
doDont: Good (from visual): the dropdown has small purple column labels, "Products" and "Use cases" (p.141), and "Resources" and "Latest blog posts" (p.142). Bad: the same items as an unlabeled two-column list with no headings.
auditCheck: Does a dropdown with 6+ items (inference) have group labels or headings? Are the items logically grouped (by product, use case or resource type)?
restyleFix: Add small column labels in the accent colour (from visual) above each group, and arrange related items together.

title: Use images in dropdowns sparingly, only for highlighted items
rule: Images give a more comprehensive visual context than icons, but "less is often more". Don't put an image next to every item. Add images only to the items you want to highlight.
why: Images beside every item overwhelm users and clutter the interface.
doDont: Good (thumbs-up, from visual): a "Resources" dropdown with a left column of 4 icon items (Blog, Customer stories, Video tutorials, Documentation, each with a short grey description) and a right column on a light-grey panel titled "Latest blog posts". The panel has 3 items, each with a small thumbnail on the left, a bold title and a truncated description, plus an "All blog posts →" link in purple. Images appear only in the highlighted column. Don't: add thumbnails to every menu item.
auditCheck: Does every dropdown row carry a thumbnail? Are images reserved for featured content?
restyleFix: Keep icons for the main items. Put thumbnails only in a featured column or panel and add a link to see all.

title: Run entrances at 200–300ms with ease-out
rule: Time entrance animations between 200 and 300ms and use a cubic ease-out so they decelerate into place. Longer than about 300ms starts to feel sluggish.
why: This range reads as responsive yet deliberate.
doDont: Do use ease-out for entering elements. Don't use linear easing or stretch entrances past ~300ms.
auditCheck: grep `transition`/`animation` durations on enter states (`duration-500`, `duration-700`, `0.5s`+); grep `linear` or `ease-in` on entrances.
restyleFix: Set entrance transitions to 200–300ms with `cubic-bezier` ease-out (e.g. `ease-out`, `duration-200`/`duration-300`).

title: Make exits faster than entrances
rule: Dismissals should run quicker than the matching entrance, e.g. ~250ms in and ~150ms out (roughly 40% faster). Symmetric timing makes the UI feel like it drags.
why: Quick exits make dismissals feel snappy.
doDont: Do shorten exit durations relative to entrance. Don't use identical in/out timing.
auditCheck: Compare enter vs leave durations in modals, toasts, menus (`data-[state=closed]:duration-*`, `exit` transition props, `leave` classes); flag equal values.
restyleFix: Set exit duration to ~60% of the entrance (e.g. 250ms in / 150ms out).

title: Respond to taps within 100ms
rule: Taps and presses need a visible response in less than 100ms; a slower reaction feels laggy even when the underlying action completes instantly.
why: Late acknowledgement makes the interface seem unresponsive.
doDont: Do make `:active`/press transitions brief. Don't let sluggish transitions hold back pressed states.
auditCheck: Check `:active`, `active:` and button `transition-duration` values; flag > 100ms on press feedback.
restyleFix: Set press/active state transitions to ≤100ms (e.g. `duration-75`).

title: Stagger list items about 50ms apart
rule: Offset each list item's entrance by about 50ms. At 30ms the items blur into one blob; at 100ms the list crawls in.
why: A good stagger lets the eye follow items without slowing the page.
doDont: Do use ~50ms increments. Don't use 30ms or 100ms steps.
auditCheck: grep `animation-delay`, `transition-delay`, `stagger`, `delay-[…]`, or `index * ` multipliers in motion code; check step is ≈50ms.
restyleFix: Set per-item delay to `index * 50ms`.

title: Reserve long bouncy motion for attention moments
rule: Attention-grabbing elements (notifications are one example) may run 500–800ms with a bounce or overshoot. Spring and bounce belong only to moments that genuinely need attention; routine entrances use ease-out.
why: Overusing bounce dilutes its signal and makes routine UI feel playful or slow.
doDont: Do reserve spring/bounce for moments that genuinely need attention (a notification is one case). Don't apply bounce easing to ordinary entrances or controls.
auditCheck: grep `bounce`, `spring`, `overshoot`, `cubic-bezier` with values >1 on routine components; do not flag deliberate restrained springs on presses/modals/confirmations (see W2-02).
restyleFix: Replace bounce on routine entrances (menus, panels, list items) with ease-out; keep springs on attention moments and on the restrained press/modal/confirmation springs from W2-02.

title: Animate accordion height with grid rows, not height:auto
rule: `height: auto` cannot transition and just snaps. Animate `grid-template-rows` from `0fr` to `1fr` on a `display: grid` wrapper, or measure `scrollHeight` and animate to a pixel value.
why: Collapsible panels otherwise jump instead of easing open.
doDont: Do use the 0fr→1fr grid technique or a measured height. Don't expect `transition: height` to work from/to auto.
auditCheck: grep `transition.*height` combined with `height: auto` / `h-auto` on collapsible panels; look for absence of `grid-template-rows` / `grid-rows-[0fr]`.
restyleFix: Wrap panel content in a grid container and toggle `grid-template-rows: 0fr` ↔ `1fr` (inner `overflow: hidden`).

title: Sync the chevron with the panel animation
rule: Give the chevron rotation and the panel height an identical duration and easing curve. A lag of even ~10 frames between them looks broken.
why: A single coordinated motion looks fluid, not janky.
doDont: Do share one duration and easing between icon and panel. Don't let the chevron fall behind the panel.
auditCheck: Compare `transition` duration/easing on the chevron (`rotate-180`, `transform`) vs the panel; flag mismatches.
restyleFix: Apply identical duration and easing tokens to both.

title: Open dropdown menus in about 150ms
rule: Make a dropdown's opening animation last about 150ms: 50ms seems abrupt and cheap, while 500ms seems slow and heavy.
why: 150ms looks smooth yet doesn't make users wait.
doDont: Do animate opening at ~150ms. Don't use no transition at all, or anything longer than ~150ms.
auditCheck: Check dropdown/popover/select content enter transitions (`duration-*`, `animation-duration`) for 0 or ≥300ms.
restyleFix: Set menu enter animation to ~150ms ease-out.

title: Build nested radii as outer minus padding
rule: For a rounded element inside another, inner radius = outer radius − padding so the curves stay concentric.
why: Concentric corners look intentional; mismatched ones look "off".
doDont: Do compute the inner radius from the outer one. Don't nest a rounded card in another with the same radius.
auditCheck: Find nested rounded containers (`rounded-xl` inside `rounded-xl` with `p-*`) and compare radii vs padding.
restyleFix: Reduce the inner `border-radius` to outer − padding (min 0).

title: Standardize corner radii on a single scale (4·8·12·16·24)
rule: Pull all corner radii from one shared scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24) rather than choosing values component by component.
why: Uniformity is what gives a UI its polished look.
doDont: Do reuse the same scale across components. Don't invent a new radius for each component.
auditCheck: grep `border-radius` / `rounded-[` values not in {4,8,12,16,24}; count distinct radii.
restyleFix: Snap off-scale radii to the nearest scale step and expose them as tokens.

title: Grow radius with surface size and fit brand tone
rule: Radius rises with surface size: ~4px tooltips, ~8px inputs, ~12px cards, ~16px modals, ~24px panels. Sharp corners feel corporate, round ones friendly; choose per brand.
why: Radius signals both size hierarchy and personality.
doDont: Do raise radius as surfaces get larger. Don't put an oversized playful radius on a serious brand, or a tight one on a playful brand.
auditCheck: Compare radius of buttons/inputs/cards/modals; flag a modal with smaller radius than an input, or a 24px+ radius on small controls.
restyleFix: Assign radii by component size per the scale above.

title: Check every text/background pair against WCAG contrast
rule: Contrast is a ratio set by the background. Aim for 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text; below 3:1 text becomes effectively invisible.
why: The same color can be crisp on one surface and vanish on another.
doDont: Do test each text-on-background pair. Don't assume a color is fine because it worked elsewhere.
auditCheck: Compute contrast for every text color against its actual background; flag <4.5:1 body, <3:1 large text.
restyleFix: Darken or lighten the text (or background) until the ratio clears the threshold.

title: Raise contrast on muted gray text first
rule: Low contrast mostly lurks in muted grays: secondary headings, card labels and navigation links often measure just 1.5–2:1.
why: Looking sleek doesn't make text easier to read.
doDont: Do darken or lighten muted secondary text until it passes. Don't leave low-contrast gray on navigation links and labels.
auditCheck: Check `text-gray-400`/`text-slate-400`/`opacity-50` on light backgrounds, and nav/label colors, for ratio <4.5:1.
restyleFix: Step muted text to a darker (light mode) or lighter (dark mode) token that meets 4.5:1.

title: Pair every color cue with a second signal
rule: Never convey meaning by color alone; ~8% of users have color vision deficiency and red/green merge. Add an icon, label, trend arrow or chart pattern next to each color cue.
why: The message must survive when the color doesn't.
doDont: Do add an icon or text to error/success states. Don't separate errors from success by red-vs-green only.
auditCheck: Inspect error/success/status elements for color-only styling (`text-red-*`, `text-green-*`, colored dots) with no icon/text/aria.
restyleFix: Add an icon (and label text) to each state and arrows to up/down stats.

title: Avoid pure black backgrounds in dark mode
rule: Build dark mode on a near-black base such as #121212 rather than #000000 so shadows and elevation stay visible.
why: Pure black flattens depth.
doDont: Do use a near-black grey base. Don't use #000 as the page background.
auditCheck: grep `#000`, `#000000`, `bg-black`, `rgb(0,0,0)` as dark-theme backgrounds.
restyleFix: Replace with ~#121212 and lighten raised surfaces.

title: Express dark-mode elevation with lighter surfaces
rule: Raise each layer of elevation with a progressively lighter grey (base, then surface, then elevated); lightness takes over the job that shadows do in light themes.
why: On dark backgrounds a shadow is nearly invisible, so brightness has to signal depth.
doDont: Do define a token per layer. Don't paint the page, cards and modals one identical dark colour.
auditCheck: Compare background colors of page, card, popover in dark theme; flag identical values.
restyleFix: Define base/surface/elevated tokens with increasing lightness and apply per layer.

title: Desaturate accents ~20% in dark mode
rule: Cut accent saturation about 20% on dark backgrounds, since fully saturated buttons and highlights vibrate and tire the eyes.
why: Toned-down accents look more refined on dark UI.
doDont: Do use a toned-down accent variant in dark theme. Don't carry the light-mode saturated accent over unchanged.
auditCheck: Compare accent values between light and dark themes; flag identical highly saturated accents (`dark:` variants absent).
restyleFix: Add a dark-theme accent token ~20% less saturated.

title: Soften text white and tier it with opacity in dark mode
rule: Don't set text to #FFFFFF on dark UI; use a soft off-white, and build hierarchy by stepping white opacity down for high, medium and disabled emphasis.
why: Pure white glares and fatigues the eyes; opacity tiers keep hierarchy without new hues.
doDont: Do use opacity levels for emphasis. Don't use #FFF for all text.
auditCheck: grep `#fff`, `#ffffff`, `text-white` on dark backgrounds, esp. for body text.
restyleFix: Use an off-white body color and `rgba(255,255,255,α)` tiers for secondary/disabled text.

title: Build shadows from three stacked layers
rule: Combine three shadows: a tight ~2px one, a medium ~12px spread and a broad ~32px ambient one, imitating how real light falls away.
why: A stack looks more physical than a single flat shadow.
doDont: Do layer several shadows whose blur and offset grow. Don't depend on one `box-shadow`.
auditCheck: grep `box-shadow` / `shadow-*` on cards and popovers; flag single-layer shadows.
restyleFix: Replace with a three-layer `box-shadow` (≈2px / 12px / 32px blurs).

title: Add subtle hover lift with border emphasis
rule: Lift hovered elements toward the viewer with `translateZ` plus about `scale(1.03)` and a soft glow, and brighten the border/shadow intensity to reinforce it.
why: A small physical reaction makes elements feel responsive without cartoonish exaggeration.
doDont: Do keep lifts to a few px and ~3% scale. Don't push scale or parallax so far it steals attention.
auditCheck: grep `hover:scale-*`, `:hover { transform: … scale(` values >1.05 and missing border/shadow change.
restyleFix: Use ~`scale(1.03)` plus a border/shadow intensity change on hover.

title: Vary parallax speed per layer, subtly
rule: Move parallax layers at unequal rates to suggest distance: slowest in the background, moderate in the middle, quickest in front (about 1x / 2.5x / 5x).
why: Unequal speeds imply genuine depth.
doDont: Do give each layer its own scroll speed. Don't push offsets so far that they draw focus from the content.
auditCheck: Check scroll-linked transforms (`translateY` bound to scroll, `data-speed`, `parallax`) for a single shared speed or extreme values.
restyleFix: Assign slower speed to back layers and faster to front, keeping offsets modest.

title: Replace hardcoded values with semantic tokens
rule: Replace raw hex colors with semantic tokens such as `var(--brand)` or `var(--error)`; intent then outlives redesigns, and renaming one token updates the entire app.
why: Tokens act as the one source of truth for consistency.
doDont: Do define each value as a named token. Don't write hex or pixel values directly in components.
auditCheck: grep `#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}`, `rgb(`, and arbitrary `[#…]` Tailwind values in components outside the token file.
restyleFix: Move values to CSS variables/theme tokens and reference them.

title: Use a numbered color scale mapped to semantic names
rule: Create a 100–900 numbered color scale so shades are systematic, and alias its steps to semantic names like brand, success and error.
why: Systematic shades replace luck.
doDont: Do define scale steps and then alias them. Don't choose individual one-off shades.
auditCheck: Count distinct colors in CSS vs the defined palette; flag shades outside the scale.
restyleFix: Define the scale and remap ad-hoc colors to the nearest step.

title: Set a fixed type scale of sizes and weights
rule: Set a fixed type scale of sizes and weights. Uniform size and weight everywhere erases hierarchy.
why: A real scale lets heading and body be told apart instantly.
doDont: Do give each level its own size/weight pair. Don't set all text at one size and weight.
auditCheck: List distinct `font-size`/`font-weight` combos; flag too few distinct levels or many off-scale values.
restyleFix: Introduce a type scale and apply by role (heading, subheading, body, caption).

title: Space everything in 4px steps
rule: Space things on a 4px scale (space-1 = 4 through space-16 = 64). Arbitrary gaps such as 7px, 23px or 11px look careless.
why: Gaps taken from a scale come across as intentional.
doDont: Do take spacing from the scale. Don't eyeball gaps.
auditCheck: grep `padding`/`margin`/`gap` px values not divisible by 4; Tailwind arbitrary `p-[7px]` etc.
restyleFix: Snap values to the nearest 4px-scale step.

title: Describe every component by variant, size and state
rule: Define each component through variants, sizes and states: buttons come as primary, secondary, ghost and destructive; sizes as small, medium and large; inputs cover default, focus, error and disabled.
why: A uniform component API keeps the interface coherent.
doDont: Do cover every variant and state. Don't leave states unstyled or built as one-offs.
auditCheck: Check buttons/inputs for missing `:focus-visible`, error and disabled styles and for ad-hoc one-off button styles.
restyleFix: Create variant/size/state classes (e.g. cva) and refactor one-offs onto them.

title: Map easing and duration to intent
rule: Use ease-out for entering, ease-in-out for moving and ease-in for leaving, with a duration scale running from 100ms for micro-interactions up to 500ms for complex transitions.
why: Intent-driven easing feels natural and consistent.
doDont: Do define easing and duration as tokens. Don't use arbitrary durations, or a single easing everywhere.
auditCheck: Collect distinct `transition-duration` and `timing-function` values; flag many one-off values or durations beyond 500ms.
restyleFix: Add motion tokens (100–500ms scale, three easings) and reference them.

title: Name tokens by role, not value
rule: Name tokens by meaning (`color-primary`, `spacing-md`, `font-body`) rather than value (`color-blue-500`, `spacing-16`), which becomes false after a rebrand.
why: Role names survive visual changes.
doDont: Do use role-based names. Don't bake literal values into names.
auditCheck: grep token/variable names containing color words or numbers (`--blue-500` used directly in components).
restyleFix: Add semantic aliases and use them in components.

title: Layer tokens primitives → semantic → component
rule: Structure tokens in three layers (primitives, semantic, component), each referencing the layer above, so one primitive edit cascades to all dependents.
why: One edit replaces hunting down 47 values.
doDont: Do reference tokens from tokens. Don't hardcode raw values across components.
auditCheck: Inspect token file for a flat list with no aliasing; count components using raw values vs `var(--…)`.
restyleFix: Introduce semantic and component aliases referencing primitives.

title: Snap stray sizes to a fixed scale
rule: Define one scale and round everything onto it, so stray values such as 13px padding or a 17px gap become 12 and 16.
why: Consistency no longer relies on guessing.
doDont: Do round arbitrary spacing and font sizes to scale steps. Don't leave off-scale values behind.
auditCheck: grep `13px`, `17px`, odd `px` values in padding/gap/font-size; arbitrary Tailwind values.
restyleFix: Replace with nearest scale tokens.

title: Implement dark mode as a token set swap
rule: Dark mode is swapping one token set for another via alias tokens, not inverting colors.
why: Same components get a deliberately different feel.
doDont: Do remap semantic tokens per theme. Don't use `filter: invert` or color flips.
auditCheck: grep `filter: invert`, many per-component `dark:` hardcoded colors vs theme variable overrides under `.dark` / `[data-theme]`.
restyleFix: Define theme token sets and have components use semantic tokens only.

title: Debounce autosave around 800ms
rule: Never write on every keystroke. Reset a timer on each key and commit one write after roughly 800ms of silence.
why: One clean save avoids request floods.
doDont: Do debounce writes (~800ms). Don't save on each `onChange`.
auditCheck: grep `onChange`/`input` handlers calling `fetch`/`mutate`/`save` without `debounce`/`setTimeout`.
restyleFix: Wrap the save in a ~800ms debounce.

title: Model the save indicator as explicit states
rule: Run the status pill off a state machine with typing, saving, saved, offline and error states, and never show "Saved" before the write has landed.
why: Users rely on the indicator more than on the feature.
doDont: Do base status on real results, updated live. Don't show "Saved" for a change the server never received.
auditCheck: Look for a static "Saved" label or boolean `isSaved` without error/offline states.
restyleFix: Add the five states and set "Saved" only on success response.

title: Queue edits offline and replay oldest first
rule: When offline, push edits into a local queue, show a badge with the pending count, and drain the queue oldest-first on reconnect.
why: Edits aren't lost and replay order stays correct.
doDont: Do queue and replay in order. Don't drop edits on network loss.
auditCheck: grep `navigator.onLine`, `online`/`offline` listeners; check for a queue and pending badge.
restyleFix: Add a local queue plus pending-count badge.

title: Never silently overwrite concurrent edits
rule: With two tabs on one document, last-write-wins can wipe out someone's work. Merge simultaneous changes or warn the user.
why: A silent overwrite can destroy an hour of effort.
doDont: Do merge or warn the user. Don't overwrite without telling anyone.
auditCheck: Look for version/ETag/updatedAt checks on save; absence suggests last-write-wins.
restyleFix: Add a conflict warning/merge prompt on version mismatch.

title: Guard unsaved work on exit
rule: If unsaved changes exist, intercept tab close with the browser's `beforeunload` prompt.
why: One dialog beats retyping an afternoon of work.
doDont: Do confirm exit with unsaved work. Don't let the tab close silently.
auditCheck: grep `beforeunload` in editors/forms with dirty state.
restyleFix: Register `beforeunload` while the form is dirty.

title: Validate on client for speed and on server for trust
rule: Use client-side validation (inline errors, green checks, 0 network calls) for instant feedback, but re-run every check stricter on the server and recompute totals from your own catalog.
why: Client requests can be forged.
doDont: Do validate on both sides. Don't trust client-sent prices or values.
auditCheck: Check API handlers for use of client-provided `price`/`total` fields and missing server validation (zod/schema).
restyleFix: Add server validation and recompute totals server-side.

title: Use optimistic UI only for cheap, reversible actions
rule: Likes, favorites and renames can repaint instantly and reconcile later; for money or irreversible actions hold the spinner until the server confirms. On response, repaint with server truth such as the real order ID.
why: Optimistic updates on payments misreport outcomes.
doDont: Do wait for server confirmation on payments. Don't use optimistic UI on irreversible actions.
auditCheck: grep `optimistic`, `onMutate`, `setQueryData` in checkout/payment/delete flows.
restyleFix: Show a loading state until confirmation and render server-returned data.

title: Use :has() instead of mirroring DOM state in JS
rule: Let `:has()` style state the DOM already holds, e.g. `.plan:has(:checked)`, `.field:has(:user-invalid)`, or `form:has(:user-invalid) button { opacity: .4 }`. Every major browser has supported it since 2023.
why: It eliminates derived React state and handlers.
doDont: Do put the rule on the container; border, label and icon then update together. Don't copy checked/invalid state into React merely to switch a class.
auditCheck: Find `useState` that only toggles a class from checked/invalid/open, and absence of `:has(`/`has-[…]:` usage.
restyleFix: Replace with `:has()` / Tailwind `has-[:checked]:` rules.

title: Prefer :user-invalid over :invalid
rule: Style errors with `:user-invalid` so they show after the user leaves a field, not on first render.
why: Avoids showing errors before interaction.
doDont: Do use `:user-invalid`. Don't use `:invalid` that fires immediately.
auditCheck: grep `:invalid` / `invalid:` in field styling.
restyleFix: Switch to `:user-invalid` (or `user-invalid:`).

title: Use CSS for layout and scroll-lock reactions
rule: Let CSS react to DOM structure: `.app:has(aside) { grid-template-columns: 280px 1fr }` for sidebars, `.grid:has(> :nth-child(n + 5))` for quantity queries, and `body:has(dialog[open]) { overflow: hidden }` to lock scroll.
why: Removes prop threading, JS counting and cleanup effects.
doDont: Do use these selectors. Don't write cleanup effects or count children in JS for layout.
auditCheck: grep `document.body.style.overflow` in effects, `showSidebar` props, `children.length` used to choose layout.
restyleFix: Replace with equivalent `:has()` rules.

title: Offer a three-state select-all checkbox
rule: The header checkbox needs empty, partial (indeterminate dash) and checked states; clicking from partial should select everything, never clear.
why: Selection scope is visible at a glance.
doDont: Do support the indeterminate state. Don't offer a header checkbox with only two states.
auditCheck: grep `indeterminate` in table header checkbox code.
restyleFix: Set `indeterminate` when some rows selected; clicking from partial selects all.

title: Name the exact count in bulk selection
rule: If select-all grabs only visible rows, offer "Select all 247 matching" and re-read the label live when filters change (e.g. 247 → 96).
why: People should act on the real set.
doDont: Do show the exact count. Don't use a vague "all".
auditCheck: grep "Select all" labels without a count variable.
restyleFix: Interpolate matching count into the label and update it on filter change.

title: Keep selection in app state with shift-click range
rule: Store selected ids in application state, not the DOM, so selection survives paging; support shift-click for ranges.
why: DOM-held selection resets when the page changes.
doDont: Do keep ids in state. Don't derive selection from the visible rows.
auditCheck: Look for `querySelectorAll(':checked')` or selection state reset on page change; check for `shiftKey` handling.
restyleFix: Move selection to a Set of ids in state and add shift-range logic.

title: Replace destructive-bulk confirm modal with a 10s undo
rule: Skip the confirm modal for bulk destructive actions: show the count, execute at once, and give a 10 second undo shown as a countdown ring that drains.
why: Undoing is quicker than answering a confirmation dialog.
doDont: Do offer an undo that repeats what was deleted. Don't depend on a confirm dialog.
auditCheck: grep `confirm(` / AlertDialog on bulk delete; check for undo toast.
restyleFix: Run action, show "N deleted — Undo" toast with ~10s countdown.

title: Offer date presets before custom ranges
rule: Presets handle ~90% of cases, so give one-click options like Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last quarter, Today and Yesterday, and keep custom ranges for edge cases.
why: Most users want to skip calendar clicking.
doDont: Do open with presets. Don't make people use the calendar for everyday ranges.
auditCheck: Look in date-range pickers for a presets list.
restyleFix: Add a preset column/list beside the calendar.

title: Make range selection legible and show two months
rule: Hover paints a live preview, first click locks start, second locks end, and edges remain draggable. Show two months side by side (three on large screens) so ranges cross month boundaries.
why: Avoids repeated "next" clicks and restarts.
doDont: Do render two months. Don't make users click "next" four times for a nearby date.
auditCheck: Check calendar for `numberOfMonths`/`months` prop = 1, missing hover preview.
restyleFix: Set months to 2 (3 on wide screens) and add range preview styling.

title: Fully support keyboard in date pickers
rule: Support the whole keyboard set: arrows traverse the grid, direct typing of a date works, Enter confirms, Escape dismisses, Page Up shifts one month, Shift+Page Up shifts one year.
why: Keyboard users get equal access and speed.
doDont: Do implement every one of these keys. Don't build a grid that only works with a mouse.
auditCheck: Check for `onKeyDown` with `PageUp`/`Arrow*`/`Escape` handling and an editable text input.
restyleFix: Add key handlers and a typed-input field.

title: Use a full-screen sheet for mobile date picking
rule: On mobile use a vertically scrolling full-screen sheet with today anchored at the top and a large confirm button at the bottom in thumb reach.
why: Popovers are cramped on phones.
doDont: Do switch to a sheet on mobile. Don't shrink the desktop popover.
auditCheck: Check for responsive branching on the date picker (media query / `useIsMobile`); popover used at small widths.
restyleFix: Render picker as full-screen sheet below the mobile breakpoint.

title: Show live contrast in color pickers
rule: Show a contrast-ratio badge while picking that turns from red to green, so failing pairs are stopped before release.
why: Checking during selection beats checking in review.
doDont: Do verify contrast as the user picks. Don't release a picker that is only a gradient and a slider.
auditCheck: Check for a contrast calculation in picker components.
restyleFix: Add a WCAG ratio badge against the target background.

title: Give pickers OKLCH, memory and alpha previews
rule: Offer OKLCH alongside hex (lightness, chroma, hue), keep recent swatches and saved palettes (last five picks), and preview alpha over a checkerboard on light and dark backgrounds.
why: Predictable adjustment, fewer repeated picks, honest transparency.
doDont: Do expose recents and a checkerboard. Don't preview alpha on white only.
auditCheck: Look for `oklch` input, recent-swatches state and checkerboard background in picker.
restyleFix: Add OKLCH fields, recents row and checkerboard preview.

title: Generate tokens from one picked hue
rule: Turn one pick into a system by generating tints and shades from a single hue, yielding ten tokens from one decision.
why: Every choice cascades through the UI.
doDont: Do derive the scale from one hue. Don't pick each shade separately.
auditCheck: Check palette definitions for hand-picked unrelated shades vs generated steps.
restyleFix: Derive tints/shades via OKLCH lightness steps from the brand hue.

title: Use bottom sheets for thumb-zone actions
rule: Put menus and primary actions at the bottom, where thumbs rest, not in the unreachable upper-right corner of tall phones. Unlike a blocking modal, a sheet leaves the page visible.
why: On tall screens the top can't be reached one-handed.
doDont: Do pin actions to the bottom edge. Don't hide frequent menus in the top right, or cover everything with a modal.
auditCheck: Check mobile layouts for key actions in top-right (`top-0 right-0`) and full-screen modals for simple choices.
restyleFix: Move mobile menus/actions into a bottom sheet.

title: Give sheets snap points, drag-to-dismiss, and scrim with scroll lock
rule: Allow the sheet to rest half-open or at full height, accept a downward drag to dismiss, and darken the page behind with a scrim while locking body scroll.
why: Adjustable height and gestures fit the need, and attention stays on the sheet.
doDont: Do add snap points and lock scrolling. Don't let the background scroll behind the sheet.
auditCheck: grep for `snapPoints`, drag handlers, backdrop element, `overflow: hidden` on body when sheet is open.
restyleFix: Add snap points, drag-to-dismiss, scrim and scroll lock.

title: Keep context menus inside the viewport
rule: Measure before opening: flip up when there's no room below, mirror left when none to the right, anchored to the cursor.
why: Menus clipped off-screen are unusable.
doDont: Do flip based on available space. Don't let menus overflow the viewport.
auditCheck: Check menu positioning for collision handling (`avoidCollisions`, `flip`, `getBoundingClientRect`).
restyleFix: Add collision-aware positioning.

title: Group menu actions and isolate Delete in red
rule: Cluster actions by purpose with dividers (Rename beside Duplicate, Share beside Copy link) and set Delete apart at the bottom in red; a dozen flat actions are just noise.
why: Grouping aids scanning and guards against mis-clicks.
doDont: Do separate groups with dividers and keep the destructive action apart. Don't dump a dozen ungrouped items.
auditCheck: Count menu items without separators (`Separator`, `<hr>`, `role="separator"`); check delete is last and styled destructive.
restyleFix: Add separators and move destructive item to the bottom in red.

title: Add a safe triangle for submenus
rule: Draw an invisible safe triangle between the cursor and the submenu so it stays open while the pointer travels diagonally toward it (hover intent).
why: Without it, submenus close as the cursor leaves the row.
doDont: Do implement hover-intent handling. Don't dismiss a submenu the instant the pointer leaves its row.
auditCheck: Check submenu hover code for immediate `onMouseLeave` close without delay/safe-area logic.
restyleFix: Add a safe-triangle or short close delay.

title: Give context menus keyboard control and mobile long-press
rule: Arrow keys step through items, typed letters jump to matches, Escape closes one level; on touch screens, pressing and holding brings up the same actions in a bottom sheet.
why: Power users and touch users need equal access.
doDont: Do support both keyboard control and long press. Don't build a menu reachable only by right-click.
auditCheck: grep `onContextMenu` without `touchstart`/long-press handling and without key handlers.
restyleFix: Add key navigation and long-press trigger opening a sheet.

title: Give dropdown triggers a 48px target with a caret
rule: A dropdown trigger should look pressable: hover state included, a caret icon showing, and a touch area of 48px; a 30px box with a faint outline fails.
why: Obvious affordance and a target that's easy to reach.
doDont: Do give it a 48px touch area, a caret and hover feedback. Don't ship a small trigger with weak contrast.
auditCheck: Check trigger height (<48px, `h-8`/`h-7`), missing chevron icon, missing `hover:` style.
restyleFix: Set `min-height: 48px`, add a caret, add hover state.

title: Flip dropdowns upward and add search past ~10 items
rule: Open the menu upward when there isn't room below, and add a search field once a list exceeds ~10 items.
why: Prevents clipping and scroll-hunting.
doDont: Do flip and add filtering. Don't let long menus clip off the viewport.
auditCheck: Check for collision handling and a filter input in selects with >10 options.
restyleFix: Enable collision flip; add a searchable combobox for long lists.

title: Wire dropdown keyboard support
rule: Custom dropdowns respond to the Down/Up arrows for moving the highlight, Enter to choose, and Escape to dismiss.
why: People who cannot or prefer not to use a pointer still need to operate the menu.
doDont: Do handle arrows, Enter and Escape. Don't build a menu that works only with a mouse.
auditCheck: grep `onKeyDown` handling `ArrowDown`/`Enter`/`Escape` on custom dropdowns; check `role="listbox"`/`menu`.
restyleFix: Add key handlers (or use a headless primitive).

title: Make command palettes fuzzy and grouped
rule: Use fuzzy subsequence matching (typing "stg" finds Settings, Storage, Staging) and group results into labeled sections like Recent, Actions, Pages.
why: Exact matching feels broken; flat lists are hard to scan.
doDont: Do fuzzy-match and group. Don't require exact substrings.
auditCheck: Check filter uses `includes`/`startsWith` instead of fuzzy (e.g. `cmdk`, fuse); check for group headings.
restyleFix: Switch to fuzzy matching and add section headings.

title: Prefill palette and keep it fully keyboard-driven
rule: Open with recent or suggested commands rather than a blank void; arrows move, Enter runs, Esc closes (and goes back one level).
why: Gives a starting point and avoids mouse return.
doDont: Do prefill suggestions. Don't open to an empty "No results" state.
auditCheck: Check palette's empty-query state renders items; check key handlers.
restyleFix: Show recents/suggestions on open; add key bindings.

title: Load async commands inline with nested drill-down
rule: For async commands, show a spinner inline and leave the palette open; nested commands get a breadcrumb, and Esc steps back exactly one level.
why: Keeps the screen responsive and preserves context.
doDont: Do spin inline and support breadcrumbs. Don't lock up the entire screen.
auditCheck: Check async command handlers closing the palette or setting global loading overlay.
restyleFix: Render inline loading rows and breadcrumb level state.

title: Start bar chart y-axes at zero
rule: Every bar chart's y-axis must begin at zero; a truncated baseline turns +4% into a fake +400%.
why: It's the most common way charts mislead.
doDont: Do start at zero. Don't crop axes to exaggerate differences.
auditCheck: grep `domain=`, `min:`, `beginAtZero: false`, `yAxis.min` on bar charts.
restyleFix: Set the baseline to 0.

title: Pick the chart form from the question
rule: Compare values with bars, show change over time with lines, and avoid pies beyond ~5 slices; the question, not taste, selects the form.
why: A mismatched form hides the message.
doDont: Do select the chart from the question. Don't use a pie once there are more than five slices.
auditCheck: Count slices in pie/donut charts (>5); check line charts used for non-time categories.
restyleFix: Convert to bar chart or group small slices.

title: Balance chart aspect ratio near 45° slope
rule: The width-to-height proportion of a chart changes how its trend reads; choose dimensions so the typical line angle is about 45°.
why: A too-flat plot hides growth while a too-tall one exaggerates it into a spike.
doDont: Do pick the proportion for an honest-looking angle. Don't compress or stretch the plot at random.
auditCheck: Inspect chart container width/height ratios for extreme values (very wide, very short).
restyleFix: Adjust height/width so the main series slopes ~45°.

title: Maximize data-ink and label directly
rule: Cut boxed legends, 3D skew, drop shadows and gridlines, and name each line directly on the chart. Every pixel left should carry data.
why: Decoration adds no information.
doDont: Do take out decoration that isn't data. Don't add shadows, 3D or gridlines that encode nothing.
auditCheck: Check chart config for `CartesianGrid`, `shadow`, 3D options, and external legends.
restyleFix: Remove decoration and place labels on series ends.

title: Use color as encoding with one hero series
rule: Highlight the key series with a single accent color, and pick categorical, sequential or diverging scales according to the data type.
why: Color should encode information, not decorate.
doDont: Do use one hero color. Don't give every series the same vivid color.
auditCheck: Count saturated colors across series; check scale type vs data type.
restyleFix: Mute secondary series in grey; accent the focus series.

title: Title charts with the takeaway
rule: Write chart titles as the conclusion ("Revenue flat since March") rather than the metric ("Quarterly revenue").
why: Readers shouldn't hunt for the story.
doDont: Do state the insight. Don't use metric-only titles.
auditCheck: Review chart titles/headings for generic metric names.
restyleFix: Rewrite titles as insight statements.

title: Use tri-state sorting on tables
rule: Sorting cycles ascending → descending → original order; a binary toggle loses the natural order.
why: Users need a way back to the default.
doDont: Do add a third click that resets. Don't ship a binary sort.
auditCheck: Check sort state logic for only `asc`/`desc` values.
restyleFix: Add a null/original state to the sort cycle.

title: Right-align numbers with tabular figures
rule: Right-align numeric columns and set tabular figures so every digit lines up on one grid.
why: Left-aligned proportional digits wobble and resist quick comparison.
doDont: Do right-align numbers using tabular numerals. Don't left-align numbers set in proportional digits.
auditCheck: grep `tabular-nums` / `font-variant-numeric` and `text-right` on numeric cells.
restyleFix: Add `tabular-nums text-right` to numeric columns and headers.

title: Freeze header and first column
rule: Make the header stick during vertical scrolling and pin the first column during horizontal scrolling, giving each a faint shadow.
why: Labels must stay within reach while scrolling.
doDont: Do make the header and first column sticky. Don't let labels disappear when scrolling.
auditCheck: grep `position: sticky` / `sticky top-0` / `sticky left-0` on table head and first column.
restyleFix: Apply sticky positioning with background and edge shadow.

title: Control row density through a single token
rule: Provide one density control that switches between a few row heights (for example 36, 48 and 60px); use zebra striping when rows are roomy and a single hairline when compact.
why: Predictable rhythm instead of guessed spacing.
doDont: Do derive density from a token. Don't set row padding ad hoc.
auditCheck: Check row `height`/padding values for one-offs; look for a density setting.
restyleFix: Add density tokens and apply to row height/padding.

title: Make the entire table row the selection target
rule: Selected rows get a full tint plus an accent left bar and checkbox, and the whole row should be clickable, not just a tiny checkbox.
why: Larger target is easier to hit and state is clearer.
doDont: Do tint and mark the whole row. Don't limit selection to a checkbox hit area.
auditCheck: Check row `onClick`/selected styles (`data-[state=selected]`) and checkbox target size.
restyleFix: Add row-level click and selected styling.

title: Lift cards ~8px over ~200ms on hover
rule: On hover, raise the card roughly 8px while its shadow grows, over ~200ms ease-out. Quicker looks twitchy; slower looks stuck.
why: Gives the card a sense of weight.
doDont: Do animate lift and shadow together. Don't make the lift much shorter or longer than 200ms.
auditCheck: grep `hover:-translate-y-*`, `:hover { transform: translateY(` and `transition` on cards; check shadow change and duration.
restyleFix: Add `hover:-translate-y-2 hover:shadow-lg transition duration-200 ease-out`.

title: Scale the image inside the card, never the card itself
rule: Scaling the entire card nudges neighbors and breaks the grid. Instead enlarge the image to ~1.05 within an `overflow-hidden` frame while the container stays put.
why: The content moves but the card's footprint stays.
doDont: Do enlarge the image inside its frame. Don't apply `scale` to the card container.
auditCheck: grep `hover:scale-*` on card root; check image wrapper has `overflow-hidden`.
restyleFix: Move scale to the `` with `group-hover:scale-105` inside an overflow-hidden wrapper.

title: Reveal card actions staggered at the bottom
rule: Reveal hidden actions (favorite, cart, share) one after another, ~60ms apart, anchored to the card's bottom; the reveal adds affordance rather than altering layout.
why: Keeps actions tidy and layout steady.
doDont: Do anchor revealed actions to the bottom edge. Don't cover the title with buttons or push them past the card edge.
auditCheck: Check hover-revealed buttons for absolute positioning overlapping title and for `transition-delay` ~60ms steps.
restyleFix: Position actions in the bottom bar with 60ms staggered delays.

title: Signal card interactivity with an edge accent
rule: A pulsing accent border or gradient sweep around the edge on hover keeps the card from looking flat and signals it's interactive.
why: Cards need a visible interactive cue.
doDont: Do add a hover edge cue. Don't leave clickable cards with no hover change.
auditCheck: Check clickable cards for missing `hover:` border/shadow/background.
restyleFix: Add an accent border or gradient edge on hover.

title: Write a plain headline naming outcome and audience
rule: Use a plain-text headline stating what the product does and a subtitle naming who it's for, instead of a gradient headline stuffed with adjectives like "Supercharge" or "seamless".
why: Adjective-heavy heroes signal nothing concrete.
doDont: Do name the outcome and audience. Don't fill headlines with supercharge/seamless/powerful.
auditCheck: grep hero copy for `supercharge|seamless|powerful|unleash` and `bg-clip-text text-transparent` gradients.
restyleFix: Rewrite headline as a concrete outcome; use solid text color.

title: Keep one accent and drop background blobs
rule: Pair a neutral background with a single splash of color, placed only on the product screenshot and primary button: one accent, zero blobs.
why: Purple gradient smears add energy but no content.
doDont: Do keep the accent for the screenshot and primary CTA. Don't add decorative gradient blobs.
auditCheck: grep `blur-3xl`, `radial-gradient` blobs, absolute gradient circles in hero.
restyleFix: Remove blobs and set a neutral background.

title: Make one primary hero button and a text-link secondary
rule: Equal-sized buttons side by side divide attention; keep one primary button and make the other a text link with an arrow, shifting emphasis from 50/50 to about 90/10.
why: One obvious primary action sharpens conversion focus.
doDont: Do downgrade the secondary action. Don't put two identical buttons next to each other.
auditCheck: Check hero for two buttons with same variant/size.
restyleFix: Convert the secondary to a link with an arrow icon.

title: Replace vague social proof with one specific quote
rule: Replace "Trusted by 10,000+ users" over grey logos with one testimonial giving name, role and a quantified outcome, such as month-end close taking three hours instead of a week.
why: Numbers nobody can verify and unfamiliar logos aren't credible.
doDont: Do feature one named customer's role and quantifiable result. Don't use counts nobody can verify.
auditCheck: grep "Trusted by" with numbers and logo strips; check testimonials lack name/role/result.
restyleFix: Replace with a named testimonial including a metric.

title: Replace icon-circle feature rows with annotated product shots
rule: Instead of three cards that each pair a circled icon with a single word (Fast, Secure, Easy), show one product screenshot with three annotations pointing at actual UI elements.
why: Pages with nothing concrete to show fall back on decoration; showing the product itself removes the generic feel.
doDont: Do show the real product. Don't build feature rows made of circled icons and single-word captions.
auditCheck: Look for 3-column grids of icon-in-circle + one-word titles ("Fast", "Secure", "Easy").
restyleFix: Substitute with a screenshot plus callouts.

title: Make the accordion header a real button with ARIA
rule: Render the header as a `<button>`, using `aria-expanded` for its state and `aria-controls` to reference the panel, so Enter/Space toggles it and a focus ring appears.
why: Native semantics provide keyboard and screen-reader support.
doDont: Do use a button with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`. Don't use a clickable `<div>`.
auditCheck: grep accordion headers for `<div onClick` and missing `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`.
restyleFix: Change to `<button>` and add the two ARIA attributes.

title: Choose single- vs multi-open by content
rule: In an accordion only one panel is open at once, whereas a disclosure allows several. Use single mode for sequential steps and multi for FAQ lists.
why: Open behavior should suit how the content gets used.
doDont: Do pick the open mode that fits the content. Don't restrict FAQ lists to one open item at a time.
auditCheck: Check accordion `type="single"|"multiple"` against content type.
restyleFix: Set the open mode appropriately.

title: Anchor the tapped header when lower items expand
rule: Reveal the new content with a stagger, and hold the tapped header in place when an item near the bottom opens, so nothing lurches under the user's eyes.
why: Stops disorienting jumps in scroll position.
doDont: Do hold the tapped header steady. Don't allow the list to jump when a lower item opens.
auditCheck: Check expand handlers for `scrollIntoView`/scroll anchoring (`overflow-anchor`) handling.
restyleFix: Scroll to keep the header fixed on expand.

title: Show drag pickup through scale, shadow and tilt
rule: A grabbed item should appear lifted off the surface: tilt it slightly, deepen its shadow and enlarge it a little, all together.
why: Signals the item has left the surface.
doDont: Do apply all three cues together. Don't let the dragged item sit flat.
auditCheck: Check drag overlay/`isDragging` styles for `scale`, `shadow`, `rotate`.
restyleFix: Add `scale-105 shadow-xl rotate-2` to dragging state.

title: Reveal drop targets during the drag
rule: Show the landing spot before release: insertion line between items, filled highlight for a column, dashed outlines for valid slots. Snap to the nearest valid slot except on free canvases.
why: Dragging should never be guesswork.
doDont: Do highlight the exact target throughout the drag. Don't demand pixel-perfect placement when snapping can handle it.
auditCheck: Check drag code for `isOver` styles and snap logic.
restyleFix: Add drop-zone indicators matched to scope and snap behavior.

title: Offer a ~5s undo after drops
rule: After every drop show a brief undo toast (~5 seconds), so a misplaced item costs a single click.
why: Drags are easy to get wrong.
doDont: Do give a short undo window. Don't let a mistaken drop stay permanent.
auditCheck: Check onDragEnd handlers for undo toast.
restyleFix: Show an "Undo" toast with ~5s timeout after drop.

title: Use named buttons for destructive confirmations
rule: Put the action itself on each button ("Delete project" / "Keep project") rather than a generic Yes/No; the verb does the warning work.
why: People skip past generic confirmation prompts.
doDont: Do label the destructive button with its own action. Don't let a vague "Are you sure?" prompt carry the confirmation.
auditCheck: grep dialogs for `Yes`/`No`/`OK` button labels and "Are you sure".
restyleFix: Rename buttons to verb + object.

title: Reserve red for destruction and move delete off the confirm spot
rule: Spend red only on destructive actions (not logout, badges, alerts), and never place a destructive button where confirm normally sits.
why: Overused red cries wolf, and muscle memory clicks primary spots blind.
doDont: Do reserve red and reposition delete. Don't put delete in the usual confirm position.
auditCheck: grep `bg-red-*`/`text-red-*`/`destructive` on non-destructive elements; check button order in dialogs.
restyleFix: Recolor non-destructive red usages and reorder dialog actions. (On conflict the playbook wins: see G-12, Cancel left / destructive right.)

title: Add friction to irreversible deletes
rule: Use a hold-to-confirm ring filling over ~300ms (early release cancels), a bordered labeled danger zone at page bottom, and a cancelable cooldown such as 14 days.
why: Gesture, location and time slow people down without a modal.
doDont: Do add a hold gesture, danger zone or grace period. Don't let irreversible deletion be one easy click.
auditCheck: Check delete flows for danger-zone section, hold gesture, scheduled deletion.
restyleFix: Move delete into a danger zone and add hold or grace period.

title: Don't use disabled buttons to block submit
rule: Disabled buttons leave tab order, mute screen readers and block pointer events, so tooltips never fire. Keep it active, validate on click, flag blocking fields and focus the first.
why: Users can't see why submission is blocked.
doDont: Do validate when clicked and focus the first error. Don't disable submit and make users guess.
auditCheck: grep `disabled={!isValid}`, `disabled` on submit buttons, tooltips on disabled controls.
restyleFix: Remove `disabled`, add click validation with error messages and focus.

title: Distinguish loading from disabled
rule: While a request runs, keep focus on the button, show a spinner and set `aria-busy` (and expose the busy status in visible/live text) rather than greying it out. Disabled labels are often pale (around 1.9:1), which makes them hard to read.
why: Greying out throws away the user's position, and the dimmed label is hard to read just when they want reassurance.
doDont: Do use a busy state. Don't treat loading as disabled.
auditCheck: grep `disabled={isLoading}`/`isSubmitting` and check `aria-busy` plus a visible/live status message; look for pale disabled labels that are hard to read.
restyleFix: Use `aria-busy="true"` with a spinner, expose the busy status in visible/live text, and keep the button focusable.

title: Acknowledge every interaction within 400ms
rule: Aim to respond inside the Doherty Threshold of 400ms: below 200ms feels instant, 200–400ms is acceptable, above 400ms damages engagement. Perceived speed beats raw speed.
why: Slow replies make users mentally check out.
doDont: Do acknowledge every interaction within 400ms. Don't hold all visual response until the server answers.
auditCheck: Check async actions for immediate loading/pressed state; look for await before any UI update.
restyleFix: Add immediate acknowledgment (state change, spinner or skeleton).

title: Use skeletons, optimistic updates and progress for waits
rule: Show placeholder skeleton shapes as soon as a screen opens, update optimistically when success is near-certain, and use spinners, progress or inline status for waits beyond the threshold.
why: Unavoidable waits still feel responsive.
doDont: Do display skeletons and progress. Don't leave the screen empty or frozen while data loads.
auditCheck: grep loading branches returning `null` or blank; check for `Skeleton`/`animate-pulse` and progress components.
restyleFix: Add skeleton placeholders and progress indicators.

title: Default to ease-out for entering elements
rule: Entering elements should begin quickly then slow as they settle (ease-out); reserve linear easing for endless loops like spinners or marquees.
why: Slowing to rest imitates physical objects; linear timing on UI that starts and stops feels robotic.
doDont: Do apply ease-out to entrances. Don't apply linear timing to UI that begins and halts.
auditCheck: grep `transition-timing-function: linear`, `ease-linear`, `animation-timing-function: linear` on non-spinner/marquee elements; check enter animations use `ease-out`/`cubic-bezier` deceleration.
restyleFix: Replace linear timing on entering UI with ease-out (`ease-out` in Tailwind); exits use the leaving curve (ease-in) per W1-27; keep linear only for spinners and marquees.

title: Add a restrained spring overshoot to presses and modals
rule: A slight spring overshoot on button presses, modals, and confirmations makes the UI feel alive and premium. Keep stiffness/bounce low so the element does not wobble.
why: A little overshoot reads as polish; too much reads as broken.
doDont: Do add subtle overshoot to presses, modals, and confirmations. Don't crank bounce until the element wobbles.
auditCheck: grep spring configs (`type: "spring"`, `stiffness`, `damping`, `cubic-bezier` with y>1); flag very low damping / high bounce values that produce visible oscillation.
restyleFix: Apply a single low-bounce spring (or overshoot cubic-bezier) to press/modal/confirmation transitions and raise damping if it wobbles.

title: Stagger list and card entrances
rule: Offset list and card entrances by a few frames each so they cascade in instead of appearing as one rigid block.
why: A cascade guides the eye and feels less abrupt than a single hard snap.
doDont: Do stagger siblings by a few frames. Don't mount a whole grid/list with one simultaneous pop.
auditCheck: grep for `staggerChildren`, `animation-delay`, `transition-delay` on list/card groups; flag lists that enter all at once with no delay offset.
restyleFix: Add an incremental per-item delay (index × small step) to list/card enter animations.

title: Reuse one small set of easing curves everywhere
rule: Use the same handful of curves for button press, card cascade, and sheet open so motion feels coherent rather than stitched together.
why: Consistent easing is a large part of perceived coherence.
doDont: Do define easing tokens and reuse them. Don't scatter one-off cubic-bezier values across components.
auditCheck: grep and count distinct `cubic-bezier(...)` / easing values across the codebase; many unique values with no shared tokens is a flag.
restyleFix: Define 2–3 easing tokens (CSS variables or Tailwind theme) and replace ad-hoc curves with them.

title: Group related items with shared visual properties
rule: Items sharing color, shape, or size look like one set, so recoloring rows can carve a uniform grid into Navigation, Content, and Actions. Line related controls up along one axis.
why: Brains group by similarity and continuity automatically.
doDont: Do style related items alike and align them on one line. Don't scatter them at mixed offsets or angles.
auditCheck: In screenshots, check that items in one function share color/size/shape and that controls share a left or center edge; flag inconsistent offsets among siblings.
restyleFix: Unify styling of related items and snap them to one alignment axis.

title: Wrap distant related elements in a shared container
rule: When proximity alone cannot group elements, a shared border or card (common region) signals belonging without moving them closer, such as settings wrapped in cards.
why: A shared region groups items even when they sit far apart.
doDont: Do wrap loosely placed related elements in a bordered card. Don't rely on whitespace alone to group dispersed items.
auditCheck: Look for related controls across a page with no wrapping container (`border`, `rounded`, `bg-*` card wrapper) and ambiguous group boundaries.
restyleFix: Add a bordered/filled card around each logical group.

title: Dim and blur the background behind a modal
rule: Blur and dim what is behind a dialog so the dialog stands out as the focal figure against the background.
why: Figure-ground separation makes the dialog feel deliberate rather than floating.
doDont: Do dim/blur the backdrop. Don't show a modal over an undimmed page where it competes with the content.
auditCheck: grep modal/dialog markup for backdrop/overlay: look for `bg-black/*`, `backdrop-blur`, `::backdrop`; flag dialogs with no scrim.
restyleFix: Add a scrim (e.g. semi-transparent dark overlay) and optional `backdrop-filter: blur()` behind the modal.

title: Derive spacing and type scales from one ratio
rule: Multiply a base unit by 1.618 for spacing (8 → 13 → 21 → 34 → 55) and type (body 16px, subheading 26px, heading 42px, display 68px), rounded to whole pixels.
why: One ratio gives gaps and hierarchy a common rhythm and removes guesswork.
doDont: Do derive scales from one base and ratio, rounded to usable pixels. Don't choose sizes ad hoc or force the ratio against an existing 8px grid.
auditCheck: Collect distinct font sizes and spacing values (`text-[..px]`, `gap-[..]`, `p-[..]`); flag many one-off values with no consistent step ratio.
restyleFix: Replace arbitrary sizes with a tokenized scale such as 8/13/21/34/55 and 16/26/42/68, rounded to your grid. (On conflict the playbook wins: see B-15/B-17, base-unit multiples.)

title: Split layouts roughly 62% / 38%
rule: Divide the screen around the golden ratio, about 62% / 38%, giving the larger panel to primary content and the smaller to secondary actions.
why: Unequal proportions create clear primary/secondary hierarchy and balanced composition.
doDont: Do give primary content the larger share. Don't force the ratio where real content needs otherwise.
auditCheck: In two-pane layouts, check widths (`w-[62%]`, `grid-cols-[1.618fr_1fr]`, flex ratios); flag 50/50 splits where one pane is clearly secondary.
