restyleFix: Set the primary pane to ~62% and secondary to ~38% of the width.

title: Use a 12-column grid with clear column ratios
rule: Start from a 12-column grid because 12 divides into halves, thirds, quarters, and sixths. Structure pages with ratios like 4:8 (sidebar + content), 6:6 (even split), or 3:9 (narrow nav + wide canvas).
why: A shared grid lets nearly any layout map cleanly and read as intentional.
doDont: Do anchor elements to shared column edges using clean ratios. Don't use arbitrary widths where 4:8 or 6:6 already fits.
auditCheck: grep `grid-cols-12`, `col-span-*`; flag hard-coded pixel widths on layout blocks and edges that do not align to a column.
restyleFix: Rebuild layout blocks as column spans on a 12-col grid.

title: Choose gutter width to match the intended mood
rule: Gutters set tone: 8px reads dense and technical, 24px balanced and clean, 40px editorial and premium.
why: Gap size changes density perception as much as columns do.
doDont: Do use tight gutters for dense dashboards and wide for editorial. Don't use one default gap regardless of context.
auditCheck: Inspect `gap-*`/`column-gap` values per layout type; flag dense data UIs with 40px gutters or editorial pages with 8px.
restyleFix: Set gutters to ~8px (dense), ~24px (general), or ~40px (editorial) to match the page's purpose.

title: Collapse the grid at breakpoints: 12 → 6 → 4 → 1
rule: Reduce columns per breakpoint: 12 for desktop, 6 for tablet, 4 for large phones, and one stacked column at the smallest widths.
why: Cutting columns step by step lets content reflow neatly.
doDont: Do cut the column count at each breakpoint. Don't keep the desktop column count on small screens.
auditCheck: grep for responsive prefixes (`sm:`, `md:`, `lg:` with `grid-cols-*`, `@media` column rules); flag fixed multi-column grids with no mobile fallback to a single column.
restyleFix: Add breakpoint variants that reduce columns and stack to 1 column on small screens.

title: Establish the grid before breaking it on purpose
rule: Intentional grid breaks (a full-width hero bleed or a pull quote pushed into the margin) only read as deliberate against an otherwise orderly grid.
why: Emphasis through contrast needs an established order to contrast with.
doDont: Do break the grid sparingly for emphasis. Don't break it before the base alignment is solid.
auditCheck: Check for negative margins / absolute offsets (`-mx-*`, `w-screen`) used in pages where other content is misaligned.
restyleFix: Fix base alignment first, then keep only one or two deliberate bleeds.

title: Keep gradients within about 60° of hue
rule: Blend neighboring hues (teal → cyan) rather than opposites (orange → blue), which create a muddy gray middle. Stay within 60° of hue travel and keep lightness moving in one direction to avoid banding.
why: Wide hue travel and lightness reversals make gradients look cheap.
doDont: Do keep hue travel under 60° and lightness monotonic. Don't blend opposite hues or go dark → light → dark.
auditCheck: grep `linear-gradient(`, `from-* via-* to-*`, `radial-gradient(` and compare end-stop hues; flag complementary endpoints.
restyleFix: Pick end colors on neighboring hues; adjust stops so lightness changes in one direction.

title: Use gradients as ambient glow, not as full surfaces behind text
rule: Put a soft radial glow behind content instead of a full-bleed linear wash over it, and keep body copy off the gradient's blended middle band.
why: Contrast can't be predicted where the colors blend.
doDont: Do use gradients as atmosphere behind content. Don't set body text straight onto a gradient's middle.
auditCheck: Find text elements over gradient backgrounds (`bg-gradient-*` ancestors) and measure contrast at the mid-transition area.
restyleFix: Move the gradient to a background glow layer or put text on a solid/scrimmed surface.

title: Add 2–3% grain over gradients
rule: Overlay about 2–3% noise on gradients to hide banding on poor displays and add texture; check on a low-end screen.
why: Smooth gradients band visibly on cheap displays; grain disguises it.
doDont: Do add faint noise and preview it on a weak display. Don't release big smooth gradients without checking for banding.
auditCheck: Look for large gradients with no noise overlay (no noise SVG/PNG, `feTurbulence`, `mix-blend` texture layer); inspect screenshots for visible banding.
restyleFix: Overlay a low-opacity (~2–3%) noise texture on large gradient areas.

title: Optically size round icons 5–8% larger than square ones
rule: Round and organic glyphs should be drawn roughly 5–8% bigger than boxy ones so they look equal; identical pixel boxes make circles seem undersized.
why: What the eye perceives as size is not the same as the measured size.
doDont: Do enlarge circular icons by about 5–8%. Don't rely only on matching bounding-box dimensions.
auditCheck: In icon sets, compare visual weight of circle-based vs square icons in the same row; check SVG viewBox fill proportions.
restyleFix: Scale circular/organic icons by 5–8% within the same container.

title: Align icons to a 24px pixel grid (16px when dense) in a uniform container
rule: Draw icon shapes on a 24px grid, or 16px in compact UI, to avoid sub-pixel blur; put every icon in an identically sized container so toolbars look even.
why: Fractional-pixel offsets soften edges, and uneven boxes make toolbars look ragged.
doDont: Do use one container size and a pixel grid. Don't allow icons to drift in arbitrary, mismatched sizes.
auditCheck: grep icon size classes/props (`size-*`, `w-* h-*`, `width=`/`height=` on svg); flag a mix of sizes beyond 16/24 within one toolbar.
restyleFix: Standardize icon containers to 24px (16px dense) and normalize SVG viewBox to the grid.

title: Keep one 2px stroke weight across the icon set
rule: Use one 2px line weight on every icon; mixing weights makes the set look pieced together from several libraries.
why: Uniform line weight is the quickest giveaway of a polished icon family.
doDont: Do keep one line weight across the whole family. Don't mix weights or pull from different icon libraries.
auditCheck: grep `stroke-width=`/`strokeWidth` values and imports from multiple icon libraries; flag values other than a single standard.
restyleFix: Set a uniform `stroke-width` (2) or replace icons from mismatched libraries.

title: Commit to fill or outline for the whole icon set
rule: Pick one approach for the whole set, either filled or outlined, instead of deciding icon by icon.
why: Random mixing lacks any unifying visual logic.
doDont: Do settle on one style, optionally an intentional active/inactive scheme used consistently. Don't alternate fill and outline arbitrarily.
auditCheck: Review icon imports/variants (e.g. `Solid` vs `Outline` suffixes, `fill=` mixed with `stroke=`) for inconsistent use in the same context.
restyleFix: Convert icons to a single style, or define a consistent state-based rule (e.g. outline idle, fill active).

title: Design all six field states explicitly
rule: A text field has default, focus, error, success, disabled, and loading states, and each needs an explicit design.
why: Any forgotten state becomes a production bug.
doDont: Do style all six states. Don't ship fields with only default and focus.
auditCheck: grep input styles for `:focus`, `aria-invalid`, `:disabled`, `data-[error]`, `aria-busy`; flag missing states.
restyleFix: Add the missing state styles (error, success, disabled, loading) to the shared input component.

title: Keep the label outside the field, not as a placeholder
rule: Show a permanent label over the input and hint text beneath; a placeholder standing in as the label vanishes as soon as typing starts.
why: Mid-entry, users forget what the field was for.
doDont: Do keep a visible label on top and helper text underneath. Don't let a placeholder replace the label.
auditCheck: grep `<input` with `placeholder=` but no associated `<label>`/`aria-label`/`htmlFor`; flag.
restyleFix: Add a visible `<label>` above each input and move hints to helper text below.

title: Make focus rings at least 3:1 contrast
rule: Field focus indicators need a contrast ratio of 3:1 or better; a gentle blue glow looks nice yet fails accessibility checks.
why: Faint focus is difficult to spot.
doDont: Do use a ring with 3:1 contrast or more. Don't depend on a pale glow.
auditCheck: grep `focus:ring-*`, `box-shadow` on `:focus` and compute ring color contrast against the surface; flag <3:1 or very low opacity glows.
restyleFix: Use a solid ring color meeting 3:1 against the surrounding background.

title: Signal errors with color, icon, and message together
rule: Pair color with an icon and text naming the problem and remedy; a lone red border goes unseen by about 12% of people with a color-vision deficiency.
why: Anyone who can't perceive the color is left out when it's the only cue.
doDont: Do pair color, icon, and written message. Don't let a red border carry the error by itself.
auditCheck: grep error styles (`border-red-*`, `aria-invalid`) and check that an icon and message element (`aria-describedby`, `role="alert"`) accompany them.
restyleFix: Add an error icon and specific message below the field alongside the red border.

title: Confirm success inside the field
rule: Show success within the field itself, where attention already is, rather than via a toast that steals focus and disappears before being read.
why: In-context confirmation is seen; toasts are missed.
doDont: Do show an in-field success indicator. Don't use a toast for field-level confirmation.
auditCheck: Look for field validation success implemented only via toast calls (`toast.success`) with no in-field indicator.
restyleFix: Add a check icon/green state in the input and drop the toast.

title: Distinguish disabled from loading fields
rule: Disabled: grayscale fill and not-allowed cursor. Loading: in-field spinner plus locked input so submissions can't double up. Don't fake disabled with 0.5 opacity, which looks like loading.
why: The two states need to look clearly different from each other.
doDont: Do lock the field and display a spinner while an async check runs. Don't rely on 0.5 opacity alone to mean disabled.
auditCheck: grep `disabled:opacity-50`/`opacity-50` as the only disabled style; check for `cursor-not-allowed` and a loading spinner with `disabled`/`aria-busy`.
restyleFix: Give disabled a gray fill + `cursor-not-allowed`; add a spinner and input lock to the loading state.

title: Validate on blur, then revalidate live after an error
rule: Check a field when focus leaves it rather than on submit or each keystroke; once it has errored, switch that field to live validation so the error clears the moment it is fixed.
why: Submit-time is too late and keystroke-time is too early.
doDont: Do validate on blur and revalidate live after an error. Don't hold all errors until submit or flag mid-typing.
auditCheck: grep `onBlur`, `mode: "onBlur"`/`"onTouched"`/`reValidateMode`, `onChange` validation; flag validation only in `onSubmit` or red errors fired on first keystroke.
restyleFix: Set validation mode to blur (e.g. `mode: "onTouched"`) with live revalidation after the first error.

title: Show positive confirmation for valid fields
rule: Use a green check to tell users a field is correct, not only when it is wrong.
why: Success is feedback too.
doDont: Do confirm correct fields with a check. Don't only flag broken ones.
auditCheck: Check validated forms for a success state (check icon, `data-valid`, green border) in addition to the error state.
restyleFix: Add a check icon/success style after a field passes validation.

title: Group long numbers into fixed chunks
rule: Insert a space every four characters so a 16-digit card number becomes scannable chunks like 4242 4242 4242 4242, and surface the card brand mark inline from the leading digit (4 Visa, 5 Mastercard, 3 Amex).
why: Unbroken digit runs are hard to read and verify.
doDont: Do format long numbers into groups and show the brand. Don't leave raw unformatted digit runs.
auditCheck: Check card/phone inputs for a mask (`inputmode`, `react-input-mask`, `imask`, `cleave`, custom `onChange` formatter); flag plain unformatted inputs for long numbers.
restyleFix: Add a formatter grouping digits 4-by-4 and an inline brand icon.

title: Keep the caret in place when auto-inserting separators
rule: After a mask inserts a separator, leave the caret immediately following the typed character instead of sending it to the field's end.
why: A caret that leaps away breaks editing in the middle of a value.
doDont: Do put the caret back where it was after reformatting. Don't allow it to leap to the end.
auditCheck: In custom formatters that set `value` in `onChange`, check for `setSelectionRange` / `selectionStart` handling.
restyleFix: Save and restore `selectionStart` around reformatting.

title: Clean pasted input and store raw values
rule: Strip dashes and spaces from pasted values and reformat to your own grouping rather than rejecting them; render the formatted value but persist the unformatted digits.
why: Users shouldn't be penalized for separators, and stored data should stay clean.
doDont: Do sanitize pasted values and save raw data. Don't error on pasted separators or store formatting characters.
auditCheck: Check `onPaste`/`onChange` handlers for sanitizing (`replace(/\D/g, "")`) and that submitted payloads contain no spaces/dashes.
restyleFix: Add a sanitize step on paste and strip formatting before submit/storage.

title: Treat paste as the primary OTP path
rule: If a code is pasted in any box, clean it of spaces and non-digits (`value.replace(/\D/g, "")`) and fill all six boxes at once. Skip one wide input; spaced codes overflow.
why: Paste is the primary path into a code field, so it has to work flawlessly from any box.
doDont: Do accept paste in any box and fan the digits out. Don't let a paste jam the field.
auditCheck: grep OTP components for `onPaste` and `replace(/\D/g`; flag missing paste handling.
restyleFix: Add a paste handler that sanitizes and distributes digits.

title: Auto-advance and backspace-retreat between OTP boxes
rule: Move focus forward as each digit lands, and let backspace on an empty box jump to the previous box and clear it.
why: Correcting a typo should never trap the cursor.
doDont: Do auto-advance and support backspace-to-previous. Don't require manual tapping between boxes.
auditCheck: Check OTP key handlers for `onKeyDown` with `Backspace` logic and `.focus()` on next/previous refs.
restyleFix: Implement focus advance and backspace retreat with refs.

title: Model the OTP as one string with mobile autofill attributes
rule: Store the code as a single string (`useState("847291")`) rather than six independent values, and set `inputmode="numeric"` and `autocomplete="one-time-code"` so the OS offers one-tap SMS autofill.
why: One source of truth is simpler, and the attributes enable native autofill.
doDont: Do keep one string state and set the autofill attributes. Don't keep an array of six separate states.
auditCheck: grep OTP inputs for `inputMode="numeric"` and `autoComplete="one-time-code"`; flag `useState(["","",...])` arrays.
restyleFix: Refactor to a single string state and add the two attributes.

title: Throttle OTP resend and give instant verify feedback
rule: Gate resend behind a visible 30s countdown to dodge a 429 Too Many Requests ban. Wrong codes shake, clear, refocus; correct ones turn boxes green with a check and "Verified".
why: Avoids rate-limit bans and makes the result obvious.
doDont: Do show a resend countdown plus clear success and failure states. Don't let an incorrect code just sit there without feedback.
auditCheck: Look for a resend button with timer state (30s) and for error/success animation on the OTP boxes.
restyleFix: Add a countdown-disabled resend button and shake/clear/refocus on error, green check on success.

title: Signal editability on hover and keep layout unchanged on edit
rule: Editable text should hint at editing with a pencil on hover or a soft background tint, and swapping to the input must keep font, size, and padding identical with the border moving from transparent to accent.
why: Without a signal, users cannot tell text is editable, and any layout jump breaks the illusion.
doDont: Do show a hover affordance and keep metrics identical. Don't leave editable text with no affordance or jump on swap.
auditCheck: Compare text and input classes (font, size, padding, `border-transparent`) in inline-edit components; check for hover pencil/tint styles.
restyleFix: Share typography/padding classes between display and input states and add a hover affordance.

title: Define consistent commit/cancel rules for inline edits
rule: Enter commits and Escape cancels; choose one rule for blur (save or discard) and apply it everywhere.
why: Inconsistent blur behavior causes lost or unexpected edits.
doDont: Do keep blur behavior uniform across screens. Don't save on blur in one place and discard in another.
auditCheck: grep `onBlur` handlers in inline-edit components and compare their commit/cancel behavior; check `Enter`/`Escape` key handlers.
restyleFix: Centralize inline-edit behavior in one component with one blur rule.

title: Save inline edits optimistically with rollback and match mode to typo cost
rule: Show new text immediately during the request; on failure revert, retain the draft, and explain. Use always-editable cells when slips are cheap, an explicit Edit action when costly.
why: Immediate feedback feels quick, and the edit mode should fit the risk.
doDont: Do update instantly, and on failure roll back while keeping the draft. Don't throw away what the user typed when a save fails.
auditCheck: Check mutation handlers for optimistic update + `onError` rollback with an error message; check high-stakes fields for an explicit Edit step.
restyleFix: Add optimistic updates with rollback and error message; require Edit mode for costly fields.

title: Give dropzones immediate drag-over feedback
rule: React the moment a file hovers a dropzone with border, glow, and copy changes — three signals before the drop.
why: Users should never hesitate over a dead-looking zone.
doDont: Do change border, glow, and text on drag-over. Don't leave the dropzone static.
auditCheck: grep `onDragOver`/`onDragEnter`/`isDragActive` with matching `data-*`/class changes; flag dropzones with no drag-over style.
restyleFix: Add an active drag state that changes border, glow, and label.

title: Show real upload progress with percent and time remaining
rule: Display percent complete and estimated time remaining instead of a bare spinner.
why: Users can decide to wait or leave.
doDont: Do show a progress bar with percent and ETA. Don't hide progress behind a spinner.
auditCheck: Check upload components for `role="progressbar"`/`<progress>`, percent and ETA text; flag spinner-only uploads.
restyleFix: Replace the spinner with a progress bar plus percent and time remaining.

title: Provide inline retry for failed uploads, per file
rule: Failed upload (even at 90%): keep the file and offer one-tap inline retry. Per-file progress and retry in a queue stop one failure stalling the other nine.
why: Forcing a restart wastes users' effort.
doDont: Do keep files loaded and retry each item individually. Don't make people re-pick files or let one failure halt the queue.
auditCheck: Look for per-file retry buttons/state and queue items with independent progress; flag a global error that clears the list.
restyleFix: Add per-item progress, error, and retry controls to the upload queue.

title: Show a thumbnail, type, and size as upload confirmation
rule: Confirm receipt with a thumbnail, file type, and size, not just a filename.
why: Visual proof shows the right file arrived.
doDont: Do show a preview with type and size. Don't treat a filename alone as confirmation.
auditCheck: Check upload list items for an ``/preview, type badge, and size text.
restyleFix: Add a thumbnail and meta (type, size) row to each uploaded file.

title: Give filter chips distinct idle, active, and disabled states
rule: Idle chips have a surface and border, active ones are filled with a check, and disabled ones are dimmed since they'd return no results.
why: When active resembles idle, the filter seems broken.
doDont: Do give the three states clearly different looks. Don't let active chips look like idle ones.
auditCheck: grep chip styles for `aria-pressed`/`data-[state=on]`/`aria-checked` and `disabled` variants; compare computed active vs idle styles.
restyleFix: Fill active chips with accent color and a check icon; dim disabled chips.

title: Refresh the result count in the same frame as the tap
rule: Update the number of results the moment a chip toggles, and provide a single clear-all reset alongside a live count.
why: A frozen number suggests the tap failed, prompting repeat taps.
doDont: Do refresh the count instantly and include one clear-all. Don't leave the number out of date.
auditCheck: Check filter handlers update count synchronously with state (no debounce delay without a loading state); check for a "Clear all" control.
restyleFix: Bind the result count to filter state and add a clear-all next to it.

title: Show combination logic: OR within groups, AND across
rule: Make filter logic legible: OR within a group widens matches (more colors, more results), AND across groups narrows them (adding a size reduces the set).
why: Users need to predict how filters combine.
doDont: Do group chips visibly and apply OR in-group, AND across groups. Don't mix logic unpredictably.
auditCheck: Review filter logic code for in-group `some`/OR and cross-group `every`/AND, and check groups are visually separated.
restyleFix: Visually group chips by category and align logic with the pattern.

title: Scroll chips in one row with an edge fade; pin active filters
rule: Overflowing chips go in one sideways-scrolling row with a fade at its right edge, not a tall wrapped block; pin the applied filters in a sticky summary strip.
why: Wrapped chips shove results down the page; a pinned summary tells users what narrowed the list.
doDont: Do keep a single scrollable row, faded at the edge, plus a sticky summary. Don't let chips wrap onto many rows.
auditCheck: Check chip containers for `overflow-x-auto`/`flex-nowrap` and a gradient mask; flag `flex-wrap` with many chips; look for a `sticky` active-filters bar.
restyleFix: Switch to `flex-nowrap overflow-x-auto` with a fade mask and add a sticky active-filter bar.

title: Never remove the focus outline without a replacement
rule: Stripping the default focus ring with `outline: none` fails accessibility unless something clearly visible takes its place.
why: Keyboard users can no longer tell where they are.
doDont: Do supply a custom ring wherever the outline is removed. Don't apply `outline: none` without a visible substitute.
auditCheck: grep `outline: none`, `outline-none`, `outline: 0` and check for accompanying `focus-visible:ring`, `box-shadow`, or `outline` styles.
restyleFix: Add `:focus-visible` ring styles wherever outline is removed.

title: Make focus rings 2px thick with a 2px offset and strong contrast
rule: A proper focus ring is 2px thick, offset by 2px, and has enough contrast to be visible on both light and dark backgrounds.
why: Thin or low-contrast rings disappear on some surfaces.
doDont: Do use 2px thickness, 2px offset, and contrast on every background. Don't use a faint or flush ring.
auditCheck: grep `ring-2`, `ring-offset-2`, `outline-offset: 2px`, `outline: 2px`; verify contrast in light and dark themes.
restyleFix: Apply `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-offset-2` with theme-aware ring colors.

title: Use :focus-visible instead of :focus
rule: `:focus-visible` shows the ring on Tab presses but not mouse clicks.
why: Keyboard users get guidance without pointer clutter.
doDont: Do use `:focus-visible`. Don't style focus rings with `:focus` and then hide them for mouse users.
auditCheck: grep `:focus {`, `focus:ring` versus `:focus-visible`, `focus-visible:`.
restyleFix: Convert `focus:` ring styles to `focus-visible:`.

title: Keep DOM order synced with visual order
rule: Focus follows DOM order, so reordering columns with CSS makes Tab jump around the page; keep visual and DOM order the same.
why: Tab order that disagrees with layout is disorienting.
doDont: Do keep DOM order matching visual order. Don't reorder visually with CSS and leave DOM order behind.
auditCheck: grep `order-*`, `flex-direction: row-reverse`/`column-reverse`, `grid-area` reordering, and positive `tabindex` values.
restyleFix: Reorder the markup instead of using CSS order, and remove positive tabindex.

title: Trap focus in modals and restore it on close
rule: In a modal, Tab cycles through the dialog and wraps; Escape closes it and returns focus to the opener.
why: Focus leaking behind the dialog or dropped on close breaks keyboard use.
doDont: Do trap focus and restore it on close. Don't let focus escape or get lost.
auditCheck: Check dialogs for focus trap (Radix/Headless UI/`focus-trap`/`<dialog>` `showModal`), an Escape handler, `aria-modal`, and focus return.
restyleFix: Use an accessible dialog primitive or add focus trap, Escape, and focus restore.

title: Make a skip link the first thing keyboard users reach
rule: One keypress on a skip link bypasses dozens of nav links; hide it until it receives focus and put it first on the page.
why: Otherwise keyboard users tab through the entire menu on every page.
doDont: Do put a skip link, hidden until focused, at the very start. Don't force keyboard users through the whole nav.
auditCheck: grep for `href="#main"`/"Skip to content" as the first body element with `sr-only focus:not-sr-only`.
restyleFix: Add `Skip to content` at top of body.

title: Add an illustration or icon to empty states
rule: A blank screen looks broken; adding a small illustration or icon shows the emptiness is deliberate.
why: Without a visual cue, an empty list looks the same as a failure.
doDont: Do include a small graphic. Don't show only a plain "No data" line or an empty page.
auditCheck: Find empty-state branches (`length === 0`, "No results") rendering only text or nothing.
restyleFix: Add an icon/illustration, a heading, and guidance to each empty state.

title: Give every empty state one primary CTA toward the next step
rule: Provide a primary action that is the next real step (e.g. "+ New project"), not "Try refreshing"; empty states double as onboarding.
why: The empty state is the best moment to teach the feature.
doDont: Do point the CTA at the next real step. Don't rely on generic "Try refreshing" as the only action.
auditCheck: Check empty-state components for a `Button`/link; flag those with no action or only a refresh.
restyleFix: Add a primary button with a task-specific label.

title: Tailor empty-state copy to the four kinds
rule: Handle the four empty kinds (filtered-out, first-run, error, no-results) separately, each with its own copy and CTA, in warm human wording, not log text ("ERROR 404 — Result set empty.").
why: Using one generic screen gives wrong guidance in at least three of those situations.
doDont: Do write human copy tailored to each context. Don't use one generic or system-style message.
auditCheck: Check whether a single shared empty component serves all cases; grep cold strings like "No items found", "Result set empty", "No data".
restyleFix: Split into four variants with unique copy and actions.

title: Preview what real items will look like in first-run empties
rule: Show a ghost preview of a real item to teach the feature before users touch it.
why: Empty states are an onboarding opportunity.
doDont: Do include a ghost example item in first-run empties. Don't show only an apology.
auditCheck: Review first-run empty states for a sample/ghost item or illustrative preview.
restyleFix: Add a dimmed placeholder item showing the structure of a real one.

title: Match the error surface to its severity
rule: Show field validation inline beneath the input, transient or connectivity trouble in a toast or banner, and reserve modals for blocking failures. More disruptive errors get more space.
why: Each error kind has a natural place; misplacing it adds friction.
doDont: Do pick inline, toast, or modal according to severity. Don't escalate a trivial validation mistake into a modal.
auditCheck: grep `toast`/`alert(`/`Modal` calls tied to form validation; flag modals for minor errors and floating alerts for field errors.
restyleFix: Move field errors inline and reserve modals for blockers.

title: Give every error a way out
rule: Every error needs a real exit — Retry, a support link, or expandable technical details — not a dead-end "OK".
why: Dead ends leave users stuck.
doDont: Do offer retry, undo, or help. Don't ship errors whose only option is "OK".
auditCheck: Review error components for action buttons other than a lone dismiss; grep `Retry`, `Contact support`.
restyleFix: Add a retry/help action to every error component.

title: Make error messages name the cause and the next step
rule: Phrase failures for people: state the cause, the reason and the next step in concrete wording instead of exposing a status code or a generic failure line.
why: A bare code or catch-all sentence gives no cause and no path forward.
doDont: Do name what went wrong and what the user can do now. Don't show only a numeric code or a catch-all failure sentence.
auditCheck: grep user-facing error strings for bare status codes (e.g. "500") or catch-all text with no cause and no action.
restyleFix: Rewrite each such message as cause + reason + next step, in plain wording.

title: Validate inline as the user types to prevent errors
rule: Live inline validation that checks each rule and turns criteria green catches mistakes before submit; keep field-level errors small, anchored to the input, and specific. (Balance with on-blur timing for format-style errors.)
why: Submit-only validation tells people they failed after the fact.
doDont: Do show per-rule progress (e.g. password criteria) near the input. Don't use a generic floating alert for field errors.
auditCheck: Check password/complex fields for rule checklists and that errors render adjacent to the input with `aria-describedby`.
restyleFix: Add a live criteria checklist and anchor error text below the field.

title: Choose loading pattern by what you know about the wait
rule: Skeleton: known content shape, wait over ~300ms. Spinner: short unknown wait under ~3s. Progress bar: wait over ~3s with known percentage, plus real meta like time remaining.
why: Defaulting to one skeleton everywhere shows little thought.
doDont: Do choose by content shape, duration, and known progress. Don't skeleton every fetch or show a full-page spinner for long waits.
auditCheck: grep `Skeleton`, `Spinner`, `animate-spin`, `<progress>`; flag full-page spinners and skeletons that don't match the loaded layout.
restyleFix: Swap patterns per context: skeleton for lists/cards, spinner inside buttons, progress bar for uploads/exports.

title: Show no loading indicator under ~300ms
rule: When a response lands in under ~300ms, show no loading state at all.
why: A flash of a loader looks like a glitch more than feedback.
doDont: Do delay showing loaders (~300ms). Don't flash a spinner or skeleton for fast responses.
auditCheck: Check loading flags are set immediately (`setLoading(true)`) without a delay/minimum threshold; look for flicker in fast fetches.
restyleFix: Add a ~300ms delay before showing the loader (and optionally a minimum display time).

title: Update the UI optimistically for reversible actions
rule: Apply likes, saves, toggles, and reorders instantly, sync server-side quietly, and roll back (restoring the count) on failure; under 400ms reads as instant.
why: People read anything under ~400ms as instant, so a spinner shown past that threshold on a simple action makes it feel broken.
doDont: Do reflect the change at once and revert if it fails. Don't hold low-stakes actions until the response arrives.
auditCheck: Check mutation hooks for `onMutate`/optimistic updates with `onError` rollback (`useOptimistic`, React Query); flag spinner-blocked likes/toggles.
restyleFix: Add optimistic updates with rollback and an error surface.

title: Don't use optimistic UI for payments or irreversible actions
rule: Keep optimistic updates for reversible, low-stakes actions. Charges, bookings, and confirmations should appear only after the server approves them.
why: Falsely reporting success on irreversible actions is expensive.
doDont: Do wait for server approval on payments and transfers. Don't show a confirmation ahead of clearance.
auditCheck: grep optimistic updates in payment, transfer, or booking flows.
restyleFix: Replace optimistic confirmation with a real pending state until the server confirms.

title: Map notification severity to toast, banner, modal, or badge
rule: Let the event's severity pick the surface: a toast for low-priority news, a banner for degraded service, a modal for a blocking error such as "card declined", and a badge for a passive unread count.
why: Routing everything to the loudest surface trains users to ignore all of it.
doDont: Do match surface to severity. Don't use a blocking modal for purely informational messages.
auditCheck: grep `toast(`, `Banner`, `Modal`, `Badge` usage and flag modals for info-level messages.
restyleFix: Re-route low-severity notices to toast/badge and keep modals for true blockers.

title: Set persistence and stacking rules per notification surface
rule: Toasts self-dismiss after a few seconds with undo; banners persist until cleared; modals block until answered; badges last until resolved. Toasts may stack; modals never queue.
why: How long each surface lingers and whether it stacks is its behavioral contract.
doDont: Do let toasts self-dismiss with undo and stack neatly. Don't line up several modals.
auditCheck: Check toast config for duration and an undo action; check for code paths that open multiple dialogs at once.
restyleFix: Add auto-dismiss + undo to toasts and serialize modals.

title: Label buttons with the reward, not the mechanic
rule: Name what the user gets ("Create my free account") instead of the system verb ("Submit").
why: Same action, different perceived value and conversion.
doDont: Do label with the outcome. Don't use generic "Submit".
auditCheck: grep button text for `Submit`, `OK`, `Click here`, `Send`.
restyleFix: Rename generic buttons to outcome-based labels.

title: Write like a person, not a system
rule: Copy should read like a helpful colleague; avoid machine phrasing such as "operation failed" in labels, errors, and empty states.
why: Wording influences whether a UI feels usable or hostile as much as layout does.
doDont: Do adopt a helpful, human voice. Don't ship machine-sounding phrases.
auditCheck: grep user-facing strings for "operation failed", "invalid", "null", "undefined", "error occurred".
restyleFix: Rewrite system strings in plain, friendly language.

title: Ask "does it block the user?" before choosing an overlay
rule: Modal only when interaction blocks; otherwise pick sheet, popover, or drawer by context. Keep modals for critical or destructive choices ("Delete account?") with full scrim and one centered decision.
why: Routine tasks become slower when something interrupts them.
doDont: Do use modals for decisions that demand an answer. Don't put routine non-blocking actions behind a modal or full scrim.
auditCheck: grep Modal/Dialog usage and review whether each is critical/destructive; flag modals for menus or quick actions.
restyleFix: Convert routine modals to popovers or sheets.

title: Use bottom sheets, edge drawers, and small popovers for non-blocking flows
rule: Bottom sheet: mobile-first default; slides up with drag handle and snap points, context partly visible. Drawer: edge-anchored panel for navigation, dimming only what it covers. Popover: trigger-anchored, ~200px.
why: Each form fits a different intent and weight.
doDont: Do tether popovers to their trigger at ~200px; use edge drawers for navigation. Don't hide navigation in an overlay that blocks the page.
auditCheck: Check popover width (~200px), sheets with drag handle/snap points, and navigation hidden inside modals.
restyleFix: Move navigation to a drawer, mobile secondary flows to bottom sheets, quick actions to small anchored popovers.

title: Use bottom tabs on mobile and a persistent sidebar on desktop
rule: Mobile primary navigation is 3-5 bottom tabs in thumb reach; desktop hierarchical content with 5+ sections uses a persistent sidebar that is not collapsed by default.
why: Visible primary destinations drive engagement and discoverability.
doDont: Do match pattern to platform and depth. Don't pick patterns by taste.
auditCheck: Check mobile layouts for a bottom `nav` with 3–5 items and desktop apps with 5+ sections for a visible sidebar; flag a default-collapsed sidebar.
restyleFix: Move primary destinations to a bottom tab bar (mobile) or persistent sidebar (desktop).

title: Keep primary navigation out of the hamburger menu
rule: Hamburgers suit secondary links; hiding primary ones there cuts engagement ~40% on mobile and ~56% on desktop. A command palette (Cmd K) only accelerates, so keep visible navigation too.
why: Few people use hidden navigation, and newcomers never find shortcuts.
doDont: Do keep primary destinations visible. Don't make a hamburger or command palette the sole route.
auditCheck: grep hamburger/menu-toggle components wrapping primary links at desktop widths; check features reachable only via a command palette.
restyleFix: Surface primary links in visible nav and keep the hamburger/palette for secondary access.

title: Use breadcrumbs only for hierarchies deeper than 2 levels
rule: Breadcrumbs justify their space only past 2 levels of depth; in flat structures they just clutter.
why: Wayfinding aids pay off just in deeply nested sites.
doDont: Do add them to deep hierarchies. Don't put them on flat sites.
auditCheck: grep `Breadcrumb` components on pages with ≤2 levels of route depth.
restyleFix: Remove breadcrumbs on flat pages; add them to deeper ones.

title: Structure landing pages as Hero, Proof, Problem, Solution, CTA
rule: Use five sections in sequence: Hero, Proof, Problem, Solution, CTA. Proof (logos, one testimonial, one hard number) follows the hero; sharpen the problem before offering the solution.
why: Visitors judge trustworthiness almost instantly, and pain drives desire for the fix.
doDont: Do put proof immediately after the hero and establish the pain first. Don't push proof to the bottom or leap to the solution.
auditCheck: Review the section order of landing pages; flag proof placed at the bottom and solution before problem.
restyleFix: Reorder sections to Hero → Proof → Problem → Solution → CTA.

title: Keep the hero to a headline, subhead, and one CTA
rule: In about 3 seconds the hero must convey what's offered, who it serves, and why it matters, using a headline, subhead, and single CTA; skip carousels or sliders.
why: Rotating slides conceal the one message that counts.
doDont: Do lead with a headline, subhead, and lone CTA. Don't put a rotating carousel in the hero.
auditCheck: grep hero sections for carousel/slider libraries (`swiper`, `embla`, `slick`) and count CTAs.
restyleFix: Replace the carousel with one headline, subhead, and primary CTA.

title: Frame benefits as outcomes, max three
rule: Sell outcomes and limit to three benefits; "save 10 hours a week" outperforms "advanced automation".
why: Results show value, whereas feature lists leave readers to infer it.
doDont: Do limit benefits to three, worded as outcomes. Don't enumerate features.
auditCheck: Count benefit items in the benefits section and check wording for outcome phrasing.
restyleFix: Trim to three outcome-based benefits.

title: Repeat the identical CTA at top and bottom
rule: Use the identical CTA, same color and same copy, at both top and bottom of the page.
why: Repeating catches scrollers who weren't ready initially.
doDont: Do reuse the exact CTA. Don't vary the label or styling between appearances.
auditCheck: Compare primary CTA label and classes in the hero versus the closing section; does not license two copies inside one viewport (header + hero): see W3-17, W3-19.
restyleFix: Make the closing CTA match the hero CTA.

title: Prefer cursor pagination when data changes often
rule: Offset pagination drifts when rows are inserted or deleted, showing duplicates or skipping items; cursor pagination anchors to a specific row and stays stable.
why: Stable lists avoid duplicates and skips.
doDont: Do use cursors for frequently changing data. Don't rely on offset paging for live feeds.
auditCheck: grep API calls for `offset=`/`page=` on feeds that mutate; check for `cursor`/`after` params.
restyleFix: Switch the endpoint and client to cursor-based pagination.

title: Truncate page links to first, last, current, and neighbors
rule: Never render every page link; show first, last, current, and immediate neighbors with ellipses for gaps. Pick numbered, load-more, or infinite scroll by job.
why: Hundreds of links overflow the screen.
doDont: Do collapse ranges with ellipses. Don't render hundreds of numbered links.
auditCheck: Check pagination components for `Array.from({length: totalPages})` rendering all pages with no ellipsis.
restyleFix: Implement a windowed page list with ellipsis.

title: Persist the page in the URL and restore scroll on return
rule: Put the page number in the URL (`?page=500`) so reloads hold position and links can be shared; also restore scroll after users come back from a detail page.
why: Users get annoyed when they lose their place.
doDont: Do store the page in the URL and restore scroll. Don't send lists back to the top upon return.
auditCheck: Check that pagination state is in the URL (`searchParams`, router query) and not just `useState`; look for scroll restoration logic.
restyleFix: Sync page state to the query string and restore scroll position.

title: Never hide primary actions behind hover
rule: Touch has no hover, so the first tap becomes a sticky hover that freezes revealed actions. Hover may surface extras only, and hover-only actions need a touch-reachable home (in the card, behind a swipe, or in a bottom sheet).
why: Touch users can't reach hover-only actions.
doDont: Do keep every primary action tappable. Don't hide primary actions behind hover.
auditCheck: grep `group-hover:opacity-100`, `:hover` reveal of buttons (`opacity-0 group-hover:`) for essential actions.
restyleFix: Make the actions always visible or move them into a menu/sheet on touch.

title: Wrap hover styles in @media (hover: hover) and use pointer: coarse
rule: Test pointer capability with `@media (hover: hover)` instead of user-agent sniffing, and use `pointer: coarse` to enlarge controls for thumbs.
why: Mouse-equipped tablets keep full hover behavior while touch-only devices dodge sticky hover.
doDont: Do rely on media queries for hover and pointer. Don't infer touch from the user-agent string.
auditCheck: grep `navigator.userAgent` touch sniffing, `:hover` rules outside `@media (hover: hover)`, and `pointer: coarse` usage.
restyleFix: Wrap hover styles in `@media (hover: hover)` and add `pointer: coarse` sizing.

title: Pad touch targets to 44px while keeping icons about 20px
rule: A 20px icon looks fine in design review yet is hard to hit; pad the hit area to 44px while keeping the glyph small.
why: Undersized targets lead to taps landing in the wrong place.
doDont: Do expand the tap area to 44px. Don't let the icon's size set the target size.
auditCheck: grep icon buttons with `w-5 h-5`/`size-5` and no padding; computed button size under 44px.
restyleFix: Add padding (e.g. `p-3`) or `min-w-11 min-h-11` to icon buttons.

title: Interpolate live cursor positions between server ticks
rule: The server streams about 10 positions per second while the screen redraws at 60fps; interpolate between ticks so cursors glide instead of teleporting.
why: Raw tick-rate rendering looks jumpy.
doDont: Do interpolate positions each frame. Don't render at raw server tick rate.
auditCheck: Check cursor rendering for lerp/spring/`requestAnimationFrame` smoothing versus direct position assignment on each message.
restyleFix: Add interpolation or a spring to cursor movement.

title: Hash user color from a stable ID and show presence
rule: Derive each collaborator's color from a hash of their ID so it persists across sessions, and show an avatar stack with an overflow counter (e.g. three faces, then +5) to signal presence.
why: Stable identity cues are tracked peripherally; presence is felt before anyone speaks.
doDont: Do hash IDs to colors and show an avatar stack with overflow. Don't assign random colors per session.
auditCheck: grep `Math.random()` used for user colors; check for an avatar group with `+N` overflow.
restyleFix: Replace random color assignment with an ID hash and add a stacked avatar presence indicator.

title: Lock selected elements and outline them in the editor's color
rule: Selecting an element should lock it and outline it in the selector's color, preventing two people editing the same shape.
why: Stops clashing edits.
doDont: Do lock and badge selected elements. Don't permit simultaneous edits of one element.
auditCheck: Check collaborative selection code for lock state broadcast and a colored outline/badge on locked elements.
restyleFix: Add a lock indicator with the editor's color on selected elements.

title: Offer follow mode for live design review
rule: Let a user click another user's avatar to bind their viewport to that user's pans and zooms, replacing screen share.
why: It makes live review in-product.
doDont: Do bind the viewport on avatar click. Don't force screen sharing for review.
auditCheck: Look for avatar click handlers that subscribe to another user's viewport state.
restyleFix: Add a follow action to avatars with a visible "following" state.

title: Show password requirements live as the user types
rule: Show the requirement list from the start, check items off as they pass, and grow a strength meter with each keystroke instead of explaining rules after a failed submit.
why: Guidance while typing spares users a penalty after the fact.
doDont: Do: Update a checklist and strength meter with every keypress. Don't: Conceal requirements until submission, then display red errors.
auditCheck: On password/signup inputs, look for an onChange/oninput-driven checklist or meter; flag forms where rules text appears only in an error state after submit.
restyleFix: Add a requirements list under the field bound to the input value, tick items as they pass, and add a strength bar.

title: Let users reveal the password and use paste or generated passwords
rule: Give password fields an eye toggle to unmask, allow pasting so password managers can fill long credentials, and ideally offer a one-tap generated password. Judge strength by length/entropy rather than a mandatory-symbol tally.
why: Masked dots hide silent typos, and blocking paste pushes users toward weaker passwords.
doDont: Do: Offer a visibility toggle, allow paste, and offer a generated password. Don't: Block paste or treat a capital-plus-symbol checkbox as proof of strength.
auditCheck: grep for onPaste with preventDefault / onpaste="return false" on password inputs; check for type toggle between password and text; check for autocomplete="new-password".
restyleFix: Remove paste blockers, add an eye toggle button (aria-label, aria-pressed) that switches input type, and add a generate-password action.

title: Make sliders fillable, fully draggable and keyboard operable
rule: Fill the track up to the thumb for an instant value read, and make the whole row draggable, not a 4px hairline. Arrows step by one; Home/End jump to extremes.
why: Precise dragging is hard, and a thin unfilled track leaves the value to guesswork.
doDont: Do: Provide a filled track, a row-wide drag target, and arrow/Home/End support. Don't: Depend on a 4px hairline as the sole target or ship mouse-only sliders.
auditCheck: Inspect custom sliders for a filled-range element, track height ~4px with no enlarged padding/hit area, and onKeyDown handling of ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End (or native input[type=range]).
restyleFix: Add a fill element sized to the value, pad the track hit area to the full row height, and add key handlers plus role="slider" with aria-valuenow/min/max.

title: Snap sliders to steps and show the value above the thumb
rule: Snap to steps with visible ticks so values like 47.3 never appear. Show the exact value over the thumb while dragging; use a two-thumb band for min/max cases like price.
why: The number appears where the eye already looks, and values stay tidy.
doDont: Do: Use stepped snapping and a live value tooltip over the thumb. Don't: Keep a slider continuous if users need clean numbers.
auditCheck: Check for a step attribute/value on range inputs and a value readout near the thumb during drag; price filters should use a two-thumb range.
restyleFix: Set step on the slider, add tick marks, render a tooltip bound to the thumb position, and use a dual-thumb band for ranges.

title: Make star ratings preview on hover and restore on leave
rule: Light up the stars up to the pointer while hovering, as a preview before committing. Hold this hover state apart from the saved rating so leaving without clicking restores it.
why: People see what they are about to submit rather than finding out afterwards.
doDont: Do: Preview while hovering and return to the saved value on mouse leave. Don't: Let the display stay frozen on the last hovered star.
auditCheck: Look for separate hover and value state (e.g. hoverValue vs value) and an onMouseLeave that resets hover; flag rating widgets with only onClick.
restyleFix: Add a hover state driving fill, and clear it on mouseleave so the display falls back to the saved rating.

title: Render fractional stars for averages and stagger the fill
rule: Show averages as partial fills: 4.4 becomes four whole stars and a fifth cut at 44%, never rounded up. On commit, fill left to right with ~30ms stagger per star.
why: Rounding up overstates quality, and an all-at-once pop feels dull.
doDont: Do: Clip the final star to the fractional percentage and sweep the fill with ~30ms stagger. Don't: Round averages upward or pop every star together.
auditCheck: Check average displays for Math.round/Math.ceil on rating values and for a width/clip-path percentage on the last star; check transition-delay steps of about 30ms per star.
restyleFix: Use a width or clip-path percentage on an overlay star layer and add per-index transition delay of ~30ms.

title: Write a descriptive search placeholder and show recent searches
rule: Write a placeholder that says what is searchable (e.g. "Search by name, SKU, or brand") rather than a bare "Search". Show recent searches the moment the field gains focus so one tap refills it.
why: The placeholder is the first onboarding and recent items cut friction to zero.
doDont: Do: Use descriptive placeholder text and surface recent searches on focus. Don't: Ship a bare "Search" placeholder with an empty focus state.
auditCheck: grep placeholder="Search" (exact, bare) on search inputs; check for an onFocus-driven recent-searches list.
restyleFix: Rewrite the placeholder to name searchable fields and render a recent-searches panel on focus.

title: Rank autocomplete by popularity and support keyboard navigation
rule: Rank suggestions by clicks, not alphabetically, with category badges; three precise hits beat ten noisy ones. Arrows navigate, Enter selects, Escape closes, and the focus ring stays visible.
why: Popularity ordering surfaces probable targets, and hidden focus breaks keyboard use.
doDont: Do: Rank by popularity, add category badges, support full keyboard control and a visible focus ring. Don't: Order suggestions alphabetically or strip the focus outline.
auditCheck: Check for onKeyDown handling ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Enter/Escape, role="listbox"/"option" with aria-activedescendant, and outline:none / focus:outline-none without a replacement focus style.
restyleFix: Add key handlers and ARIA combobox roles, sort suggestions by usage score, and restore a visible focus-visible ring.

title: Make empty search results a way forward
rule: When a search finds nothing, present popular searches, category shortcuts or alternative spellings, helping users recover just as they would otherwise abandon.
why: An empty dead end is where people bounce.
doDont: Do: Give suggestions and category links when results are empty. Don't: Leave only a plain "No matches" line.
auditCheck: Find empty/no-results branches in search components and check they render more than a single text line (links, suggestions).
restyleFix: Add popular searches, category chips and a spell-suggestion line to the empty state.

title: Chunk long forms into steps with visible progress
rule: Split long forms into meaningful groups (Personal, Shipping, Payment, Review), not arbitrary counts: three fields are easy, twelve cause exhausting scrolling. Add one progress cue: bar, numbered dots or labels.
why: Chunking reduces mental load, and visible progress shows the finish nearing.
doDont: Do: Group steps by context and include a progress indicator. Don't: Pile twelve fields into one scrolling wall or split at arbitrary counts.
auditCheck: Count inputs per form/page (flag around 12 or more in one view); check for a stepper/progress element in multi-step flows.
restyleFix: Break the form into semantic steps and add a progress bar, dots, or labeled steps.

title: Validate inside each step and keep entered data
rule: Validate fields within their own step when Next is clicked, show inline errors immediately instead of rejecting at the final screen, and focus the first invalid field. Persist state on every step change so Back and refresh keep what was entered.
why: Losing a form or surfacing step-one errors on step four loses the user.
doDont: Do: Validate per step, show inline errors, and persist data across steps and refresh. Don't: Surface early errors at the end or discard input on Back/refresh.
auditCheck: Check each step validates on Next-click (not via a disabled Next; see W1-94), keeps entered data, and flags and focuses the first invalid field; check persistence (localStorage/sessionStorage/URL/state store) across steps.
restyleFix: Keep Next enabled, validate the step on click with a per-step schema, keep entered data, show inline messages and focus the first invalid field (see W1-94); persist form state on each step change.

title: Build toggles with fixed proportions and a keyboard-accessible semantics
rule: Make the rail 2x the knob's diameter, padded by the knob's radius so it stays centred in both states. Space toggles when focused; show a visible focus ring; expose the state through either role="switch" with aria-checked on a button, or a native checkbox using its own checked state (never both).
why: Steady proportions look polished, and proper semantics let keyboard and screen-reader users operate it.
doDont: Do: Use a button with role="switch" and aria-checked, or a native checkbox with its native checked state; add Space support and a visible focus ring. Don't: Ship a toggle that reacts only to mouse clicks, or put aria-checked on a native checkbox.
auditCheck: grep custom toggles for role="switch" + aria-checked on a button, or a native input type=checkbox without aria-checked (not a bare div onClick), and focus-visible styles; check rail width ≈ 2× knob size.
restyleFix: Use either a button with role="switch" and aria-checked, or a native checkbox relying on its checked state; add focus-visible ring and correct rail/knob sizing.

title: Animate toggle flips over ~250ms and handle async state
rule: Transition rail color, knob translateX, knob shadow and label together over ~250ms ease-out. Async: flip optimistically, show a knob loader while pending, revert with shake and error toast on failure.
why: An abrupt jump looks broken, and a switch without a spinner seems stuck during a request.
doDont: Do: Morph all four properties together, with a pending spinner and failure rollback. Don't: Snap the knob instantly or leave network status unclear.
auditCheck: Check toggle CSS for transition on background-color and transform with ~250ms ease-out; flag toggles with no transition; check async toggles for pending and error rollback handling.
restyleFix: Add transition-all duration-[250ms] ease-out to rail/knob, add pending spinner state and rollback on error.

title: Space items inside a group more tightly than between groups
rule: Close elements read as one group, so keep spacing within groups tighter than between them: about 12px between related form fields, about 40px between sections. Equal spacing flattens hierarchy.
why: Viewers infer relationships purely from distance.
doDont: Do: Keep spacing tight inside groups and larger at section breaks. Don't: Space every element identically.
auditCheck: Compare gap/margin values within and between groups (e.g. gap-3 within vs gap-10 between); flag forms where field and section gaps are identical.
restyleFix: Set related fields to ~12px spacing and section breaks to ~40px. (On conflict the playbook wins: see A-16, label 12px / next field 32px.)

title: Group nav and toolbar items by function and let whitespace do the dividing
rule: Group controls by function (navigate, actions, system) and split long lists like eight sidebar links into labeled groups such as Dashboard, Management and Account. Use whitespace for grouping before reaching for borders, boxes or dividers.
why: Spacing and labeled groups make flat lists scannable without extra lines.
doDont: Do: Group by meaning and rely on spacing first. Don't: Use boxes and dividers where a larger gap says the same thing.
auditCheck: Check sidebars/toolbars for a single evenly spaced list of many items and for border/divider elements between every group.
restyleFix: Split long nav lists into labeled sections and swap dividers for larger gaps.

title: Stack size, color, contrast, whitespace and weight to create one focal point
rule: Make the primary element about 2x body size with more padding than neighbours, supported by weight: 800 headings, 400 body, 300 captions. Combine properties; none carries a layout alone.
why: Stacked cues create a clear entry point and reading order.
doDont: Do: Make the headline about double body size, combining size with weight, contrast and spacing. Don't: Depend on size alone or give everything equal emphasis.
auditCheck: Compare heading to body font sizes (ratio near 2x), font-weight spread across headings/body/captions, and padding of the hero versus secondary items.
restyleFix: Scale the headline to ~2x body, set weights 800/400/300 by role, and give the hero extra padding.

title: Reserve one accent color for the single key action
rule: Keep the interface neutral; reserve one accent for the one action you want taken. Contrast pairs: bold white headings over muted copy, filled primary beside ghost secondary.
why: Many colors turn hierarchy into noise.
doDont: Do: Use one accent for the primary action and ghost-style secondaries. Don't: Give each element its own color.
auditCheck: Count distinct accent/hue classes in a view; check for more than one filled primary-style button per view.
restyleFix: Neutralize secondary elements, make secondary buttons ghost/outline, and keep the accent only on the primary CTA. (On conflict the playbook wins: see E-31, avoid pure white; use off-white for headings.)

title: Isolate one element against a uniform baseline
rule: Make one item differ: enlarge the pricing target with a "Most Popular" badge and dim others, or lift a lone CTA with color, scale and glow over quiet nav links.
why: Visually distinct items get noticed and remembered; contrast needs a uniform baseline.
doDont: Do: Set the one target action apart through scale, color and a badge among quiet neighbours. Don't: Offer identical options and expect users to choose the intended one.
auditCheck: In pricing/option card sets check that one card differs in scale/badge/elevation; flag sets where all cards are identical or where several are highlighted.
restyleFix: Pick one target card/CTA, add scale, badge and glow, and mute the rest.

title: Limit emphasis to one element and never rely on color alone
rule: Highlight one element per view (featured plan, main CTA or form button); two or three cancel each other out. Add scale, elevation and glow to color so color-blind users notice.
why: Competing emphasis cancels isolation, and color-only contrast fails some users.
doDont: Do: Emphasise one element and pair color with scale or elevation. Don't: Highlight several items or depend on color alone.
auditCheck: Count emphasized elements per view (primary buttons, highlighted cards); check whether the emphasized state differs by more than hue (size, shadow, badge).
restyleFix: Demote extra highlights and add scale/elevation/badge to the one standout.

title: Put the most important items at the start and end of a sequence
rule: U-shaped recall: navbars begin with logo, end with primary CTA; landing pages open with the best USP, close with proof (testimonials, metrics, guarantees); onboarding hooks first, pays off last.
why: Items in the middle of a sequence are forgotten.
doDont: Do: Anchor key items at the start and end of lists or flows. Don't: Hide important CTAs or information midway.
auditCheck: In navbars check the primary CTA is the last item and the logo is first; on landing pages check the USP is at the top and flag proof buried mid-page (proof directly after the hero is fine; see W2-74).
restyleFix: Reorder nav so the primary CTA/logo bookend it, and move buried mid-page proof to the hero-adjacent slot or the page close (see W2-74).

title: Engineer a deliberate peak and a strong ending in flows
rule: Users judge a flow by its most intense moment and its final moment, so design at least one intentional peak (surprise upgrade, free perk, delight) and end on a celebration, not a flat confirmation. One delight outweighs five neutral steps.
why: Memory stores the peak and the end rather than the average.
doDont: Do: Add a peak partway through and celebrate on the last screen. Don't: Spread effort evenly while neglecting the finish.
auditCheck: Review the final screen of each flow (success/confirmation pages) for a plain text-only state; check for any celebratory element or next-step.
restyleFix: Upgrade the success screen with a celebratory visual, clear summary and next action.

title: Audit the last interaction of every flow for friction
rule: A broken, error-ridden or dead-end last step ruins how an otherwise smooth experience is remembered, so verify that each flow finishes without friction.
why: The ending carries outsized weight in what users recall.
doDont: Do: Review the final interaction of every flow. Don't: Let a flow close on friction, errors or a dead end.
auditCheck: Inspect last-step handlers for unhandled errors, missing success state, and screens with no next action or link.
restyleFix: Add error recovery to the final step and a next-step CTA to the confirmation.

title: Use an open loop only for outcomes users want
rule: A visible gap (progress stuck at 80%, one unchecked onboarding box) keeps an unfinished task in mind, but only for goals users care about, like profile completion, not fake progress.
why: Unfinished tasks stay in active memory; completed ones are dropped.
doDont: Do: Show noticeable remaining progress tied to a goal the user wants. Don't: Close every loop at 100% or invent progress, such as a reading bar in a marketing email.
auditCheck: Check onboarding/profile components for a progress meter with remaining items; flag progress bars on non-task content.
restyleFix: Add a profile/onboarding completion meter with the next unchecked step highlighted.

title: Give cards generous padding, radius and a clear type hierarchy
rule: Generous padding signals intent: use 40px instead of a cramped 12px, plus a 24px border-radius. Title at weight 600, ~38px; body smaller at ~55% opacity so the title wins.
why: Spacing and type account for most of the difference between cheap-looking and premium cards.
doDont: Do: Use ~40px padding, ~24px radius, a 600-weight title and ~55% opacity description. Don't: Squeeze content to the edges with tiny padding, near-zero radius or equal title/body weight.
auditCheck: Check card classes for p-3/12px padding with rounded-none/sm, and title/body with the same font-weight and opacity.
restyleFix: Raise card padding to ~40px, radius to ~24px, set title 600 at ~38px, and body ~55% opacity.

title: Layer a tight and a soft shadow plus a ~12% hairline border on cards
rule: Stack two shadows — a tight, darker one for contrast and a wide, soft one for ambient elevation — and add a hairline border at about 12% opacity to define the card edge on a dark background.
why: Two layers read as believable depth and the border keeps the edge crisp.
doDont: Do: Combine a tight and a soft ambient shadow with a ~12% border. Don't: Use one flat shadow or no edge definition on dark surfaces.
auditCheck: grep box-shadow values on cards for a single shadow and check border color alpha around 0.12 (e.g. border-white/10–12).
restyleFix: Replace single shadow with two comma-separated layers and add a 1px border at ~12% opacity. (On conflict the playbook wins: see D-05, soft diffuse shadows over a tight dark one.)

title: Give clickable cards a hover lift
rule: On hover, raise the card about 8px with translateY and make the shadow deeper, signalling that it can be clicked. Do not scale the card container (see W1-77).
why: A hover response supplies the last bit of polish and affordance.
doDont: Do: Apply ~8px lift and a deeper shadow on hover. Don't: Give interactive cards no hover feedback, or scale the card itself.
auditCheck: Check clickable cards for :hover / hover: rules with translateY(-8px) or a shadow change; flag scale on the card root (see W1-77).
restyleFix: Add hover:-translate-y-2 with a stronger shadow and a transition; do not scale the card container (see W1-77; scale the inner image instead).

title: Build elevation from three layered shadows and use it as hierarchy
rule: Layer a tight contact shadow (~0 1px 3px), a mid-range and a wide diffuse shadow. Elevation signals importance: reserve it for key elements, e.g. lifted premium plan, flat basic.
why: Layered shadows look physical, and elevation conveys priority.
doDont: Do: Use three shadow layers and keep the highest elevation for the most important elements. Don't: Use one flat drop shadow everywhere or treat shadows as decoration.
auditCheck: Check box-shadow declarations for a single layer and for identical shadows across all surfaces.
restyleFix: Define an elevation scale with three-layer shadows and apply the highest level only to key elements.

title: Use a brand-tinted glow and optional 3D tilt for premium elevation
rule: Add a low-opacity blurred glow in an accent hue matching the product domain (creative tools purple, fintech blue, health green). Perspective with small rotateX and translateZ adds 3D depth.
why: Tinted glows give branded polish that plain black shadows can't.
doDont: Do: Tint the glow with the brand accent. Don't: Rely on black shadows alone for a branded product.
auditCheck: Check shadow colors for rgba(0,0,0,…) only; look for perspective/rotateX/translateZ on lifted surfaces.
restyleFix: Add a low-opacity accent-colored glow layer to the shadow stack.

title: Build depth from background values and a hairline, not shadows
rule: For a flat engineered look, skip shadows; use three background tones (base, surface, raised) divided by a 1px border of 8% white. Hover shifts surface value, not elevation.
why: Flat surfaces feel engineered, whereas shadows feel decorated.
doDont: Do: Use three background values, an rgba white 8% hairline, and surface-value hover. Don't: Separate rows, panels or the sidebar with drop shadows.
auditCheck: grep shadow-* / box-shadow on rows, panels and sidebars in dense dark UIs; check for border-white/[0.08] and hover:bg-* changes.
restyleFix: Remove shadows, define three bg tokens, add 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.08) borders and hover surface shifts.

title: Make dense UIs compact with one accent and grey status icons
rule: Compact UIs signal competence: 13px text, 32px rows, -1% tracking fit 14 issues versus 8. One indigo accent on selected row and primary button; status as grey icons, not pills.
why: Seven colors reduce to one, and the UI looks intentional.
doDont: Do: Use 13px text, 32px rows, one accent and grey status icons. Don't: Mark status or priority with colored pills where a grey icon conveys it.
auditCheck: Check data-list row heights (~32px), font-size 13px, count of distinct accent colors, and colored badge/pill status components.
restyleFix: Compact rows, apply -0.01em tracking, replace colored pills with grey icons and limit the accent to selection and primary. Dense tool UIs only. (On conflict the playbook wins: see F-06, 16px body.)

title: Align labels left and numbers right on a 4px grid
rule: Use a 4px grid and 16px icons centred on the text line. Labels and ids align left; numbers and dates align right; nothing is centred.
why: Correct alignment goes unnoticed; wrong alignment stands out.
doDont: Do: Left-align text, right-align numbers/dates, and centre icons with the text line. Don't: Centre table cells or let icons drift off the text.
auditCheck: Check table cells for text-center on data columns, numeric columns without text-right/tabular-nums, and spacing values off the 4px scale.
restyleFix: Right-align numeric/date columns, left-align labels, and snap spacing to multiples of 4px.

title: Fix z-index with position and stacking contexts, not bigger numbers
rule: z-index needs position (relative, absolute, fixed or sticky). A child can't escape its parent's stacking context, so 9999 cannot win what the parent lost; values rank siblings per context.
why: Escalating from 9999 to 99999 hides an unexpected stacking context.
doDont: Do: Add position before z-index and locate the parent stacking context. Don't: Keep raising to z-index: 9999 to push a child over another branch.
auditCheck: grep z-index values at or above 999; flag z-index only on plain position: static block elements (z-index does apply to flex/grid children even when static, so exclude them); count distinct z-index values for an ad hoc scale.
restyleFix: Remove arbitrary huge values, add position: relative where needed and define a small z-index scale.

title: Contain component layers with isolation: isolate
rule: isolation: isolate creates a new stacking context in one declaration, so inner layers can't leak out and collide with the page. DevTools' Layers panel shows the real 3D stack.
why: Containing stacking removes any need for global z-index escalation.
doDont: Do: Apply isolation: isolate to components with inner layering. Don't: Presume that a larger z-index always prevails.
auditCheck: Check components with internal z-index children for isolation: isolate / the isolate Tailwind class.
restyleFix: Add isolate to the component root.

title: Delay hover tooltips ~300ms and anchor them with an arrow
rule: Hold a hover tooltip back for about 300ms so accidental cursor passes don't open it, and add an arrow pointing at the trigger so the target is clear.
why: Instant tooltips without an anchor are noisy and ambiguous.
doDont: Do: Delay ~300ms and add an arrow toward the trigger. Don't: Pop up immediately whenever the cursor brushes past.
auditCheck: Check tooltip components for delay props (delayDuration/delay ≈ 300) and an arrow element; flag 0ms delays.
restyleFix: Set the open delay to 300ms and render an arrow.

title: Flip tooltips near edges and allow every dismissal route
rule: Near a viewport edge, show the tooltip on the opposite side to avoid clipping, and dismiss it on mouse leave, Escape, blur (focus leaving) and tapping elsewhere.
why: Clipped or undismissable tooltips harm readability and accessibility.
doDont: Do: Flip near edges and dismiss on mouse leave, Escape, blur and outside tap. Don't: Let tooltips clip off-screen or close only on mouse leave.
auditCheck: Check tooltip positioning (flip/collision handling) and keydown Escape/onBlur handlers.
restyleFix: Enable flip/collision avoidance and add Escape, blur and outside-click handlers.

title: Keep tooltip copy to one short sentence
rule: Limit tooltip width to about 300px and a single sentence; a paragraph of documentation belongs elsewhere.
why: Long tooltip text is hard to read and vanishes when the mouse moves.
doDont: Do: Use one sentence, at most ~300px wide. Don't: Stuff multi-line, documentation-sized text into a tooltip.
auditCheck: Check tooltip max-width (~300px/max-w-xs) and content length.
restyleFix: Shorten the text or move it to a popover/help page.

title: Position toasts away from the content center
rule: Place toasts bottom-right on desktop and at the top edge on mobile; never the screen center, which covers active content and blocks clicks.
why: Central toasts block the content users are working on.
doDont: Do: Anchor bottom-right on desktop and top on mobile. Don't: Put toasts in the screen center.
auditCheck: Check toast container position classes (bottom-right, top-center on mobile) and absence of centered fixed toasts.
restyleFix: Move the toast viewport to bottom-right (desktop) and top (mobile).

title: Match toast dismiss timing to severity and cap the stack at three
rule: Auto-dismiss info after about 4s, warnings after about 7s, and keep critical errors until acknowledged. Show at most 3 toasts, newest at the bottom, older floating up and out, and queue the rest.
why: Timing and caps match urgency and avoid a pile-up.
doDont: Do: Use ~4s info, ~7s warning, sticky errors, and max 3 visible. Don't: Auto-dismiss critical errors or show more than three toasts.
auditCheck: grep toast duration options (≈4000, ≈7000) and Infinity for errors; check visibleToasts/limit ≤ 3.
restyleFix: Set per-severity durations, make errors persistent, and set a toast limit of 3 with a queue.

title: Give toasts an exit, hover-pause and non-color cues
rule: Provide a close button (desktop), swipe-dismiss (mobile) and a hover-paused timer. Pair color-coded types with an icon and accent border; about 6% of users can't distinguish the colors.
why: Users need control of timing, and color alone is insufficient.
doDont: Do: Pause the countdown on hover and pair color with an icon and accent border. Don't: Depend on color alone to convey toast type.
auditCheck: Check toasts for a close button, pauseOnHover behavior, swipe handling, and an icon per type.
restyleFix: Add a close button, pause-on-hover, and per-type icon and left border.

title: Prefer undo with a visible countdown over "Are you sure?" dialogs
rule: Run the action immediately and offer a timed undo with a visible clock (draining ring or bar) in place of confirmation dialogs. Keep the window long enough to react.
why: Undo penalises nobody; confirmations penalise everyone for one person's slip.
doDont: Do: Execute at once and show an undo toast with a countdown. Don't: Put every destructive action behind a confirmation prompt.
auditCheck: grep window.confirm / confirm dialogs on reversible deletes and check undo toasts for a timer indicator.
restyleFix: Replace confirm dialogs on reversible actions with an undo toast with a draining bar.

title: Soft-delete with a recovery window and reserve heavy friction for irreversible actions
rule: Set a deleted flag and keep items in trash for thirty days before purging; save type-to-confirm friction (like GitHub requiring the repo name) for truly irreversible actions. Delayed send (Gmail's ten seconds) and an undo stack with Cmd+Z extend the same idea.
why: Deletion should be a state, not an event, and friction should sit only where there is no way back.
doDont: Do: Soft-delete with a recovery window and use type-to-confirm only for irreversible actions. Don't: Hard-delete from the database on click.
auditCheck: Check delete handlers for hard DELETE vs deleted_at/deletedAt flags and for a trash view; check irreversible flows for type-to-confirm.
restyleFix: Add a deleted_at flag with a 30-day purge and require typing the resource name for permanent deletion.

title: Quarantine destructive settings and match apply model to stakes
rule: Commit light toggles instantly with a saved confirmation; identity fields like email get Save/Cancel. Wall delete off at the page bottom, gated by typing the exact resource name.
why: Matching commit style to blast radius prevents accidents.
doDont: Do: Apply low-stakes toggles instantly, require explicit save for identity, and type-to-confirm for delete. Don't: Allow irreversible actions on one unprotected click.
auditCheck: Check destructive buttons for a confirm input requiring the resource name, a danger-zone section at page bottom, and Save/Cancel on identity fields.
restyleFix: Move delete into a bottom danger zone with type-the-name confirmation.

title: Organize settings by task, searchable, with reset per changed value
rule: Group by user task, not data model, so twenty flat rows become three scannable sections; add search; mark changed values with a modified indicator and per-setting reset; collapse advanced options.
why: Task grouping and search keep the common path short.
doDont: Do: Group by task, add search, show modified markers with reset, and collapse advanced options. Don't: Dump every option into one flat schema-ordered list or bury settings in nested menus.
auditCheck: Check settings pages for a search input, section headings, and reset controls; count rows in an ungrouped list.
restyleFix: Split settings into task sections, add a search field, reset links and an advanced accordion.

title: Give swipe actions discoverability, friction and a visible fallback
rule: Hint via peek or onboarding nudge; reveal destructive buttons on partial swipe, committing by tap (or full swipe plus undo toast). Add a visible fallback: long-press menu or detail-view button.
why: Swipe is hidden UI, and an instant full-swipe delete risks losing data.
doDont: Do: Pair swipe actions with an undo window and a visible fallback path. Don't: Make swipe the sole route or let a full swipe delete immediately.
auditCheck: Check swipe components for an undo handler and an equivalent button/menu action in the row or detail view.
restyleFix: Add an overflow menu or detail button, and an undo toast for swipe deletes.

title: Color-code swipe actions by consequence and cap actions per side
rule: Use surface tones for neutral actions and red for destructive ones, keep colors and left/right meanings uniform in every list, and limit each side to two actions.
why: Past two actions, users can't form muscle memory.
doDont: Do: Keep colors and left/right meanings uniform app-wide. Don't: Offer over two actions on either side.
auditCheck: Count swipe actions per side and compare action colors/directions across list components.
restyleFix: Reduce to two actions per side and standardize the color mapping.

title: Slide the tab indicator and fade content instead of cutting
rule: Glide the active indicator with a spring instead of jumping, timed to the content fade. Fade out, wait about 80ms, fade in, and equalise panel heights to prevent shifting.
why: Hard cuts and layout shifts make tab changes feel abrupt.
doDont: Do: Slide the indicator and fade panels of equal height. Don't: Swap content with a hard cut.
