auditCheck: Check tab indicators for transition/layoutId/spring on position, and panels for opacity transition and min-height.
restyleFix: Add an animated indicator and a fade transition with ~80ms pause and equal panel heights.

title: Scroll overflowing tabs and make them keyboard operable
rule: When tabs overflow, scroll sideways with edge fades and desktop chevron buttons, not wrapping. Arrows move between tabs, Home first, End last, Tab exits to next focusable group.
why: Wrapping breaks the row, and keyboard support is basic.
doDont: Do: Scroll overflow with fades and support arrow/Home/End keys. Don't: Let an overflowing tab row spill onto a second line.
auditCheck: Check tab lists for flex-wrap, overflow-x-auto with fade masks, role="tablist"/"tab" and onKeyDown for arrows/Home/End.
restyleFix: Switch to nowrap overflow-x scroll with edge fades and add roving tabindex key handling.

title: Keep the focus ring and active tab in different colors
rule: Never let the focus ring and the active state share a color, otherwise keyboard users cannot tell where they are versus what is selected.
why: Distinct signals separate focus from selection.
doDont: Do: Use distinct colors for focus and active. Don't: Reuse the same color for both.
auditCheck: Compare focus-visible ring color with the active tab color.
restyleFix: Change the focus ring to a contrasting color or offset ring distinct from the active indicator.

title: Adapt tabs to mobile with segmented controls or a sheet
rule: On mobile, use a segmented control when there are fewer than 5 tabs and a bottom sheet when there are more than 5; don't just shrink the desktop bar.
why: A shrunken desktop bar is hard to use on mobile.
doDont: Do: Choose a segmented control below 5 tabs, a bottom sheet above 5. Don't: Carry the desktop tab bar to mobile in smaller form.
auditCheck: Check mobile breakpoints for a different tab component and count tabs per bar.
restyleFix: Add a mobile variant: segmented control or bottom sheet by tab count.

title: Use skeletons that mirror the final layout and shimmer
rule: Mimic what's coming: avatar circle, text bars, image block, with shimmer; a static skeleton looks broken. Use true content dimensions, since a layout-changing skeleton is worse than a spinner.
why: Skeletons let users begin parsing the layout during loading.
doDont: Do: Shape skeletons like the final layout and animate them. Don't: Use a static or mismatched skeleton.
auditCheck: Check skeleton components for animate-pulse/shimmer keyframes and matching dimensions with loaded components; check for layout shift (CLS) on load.
restyleFix: Rebuild the skeleton from the real component's dimensions and add a shimmer animation.

title: Apply skeletons only where they help and render user actions optimistically
rule: Show skeletons for under ~2 seconds, then partial content; skip them under 300ms; never mix spinners and skeletons in a view. Make user actions (posting, liking) optimistic, reconciling afterwards.
why: A flashing skeleton is noise, and a spinner says nothing about what or how long.
doDont: Do: Use skeletons for meaningful waits and optimistic UI for user actions. Don't: Show skeletons for sub-300ms loads or mix spinners with skeletons in a view.
auditCheck: Check for spinners and skeletons in the same view, skeletons without a delay threshold, and mutation handlers without optimistic updates.
restyleFix: Add a ~300ms show-delay, unify on skeletons per view and add optimistic mutation updates.

title: Drive scroll effects with CSS scroll and view timelines
rule: Use `animation-timeline: scroll()` to tie an animation to scroll position and `view()` to animate individual elements as they enter the viewport, with `animation-range` setting the exact trigger points (entry, exit, or in between). This needs no JavaScript or IntersectionObserver.
why: The browser handles scroll-linked motion natively, replacing roughly 30 lines of JS and a scroll listener for effects like parallax.
doDont: Do: Use animation-timeline: scroll()/view() for scroll-linked reveals and parallax. Don't: Hand-roll them with scroll listeners and getBoundingClientRect() or add a JS animation library for effects CSS covers.
auditCheck: grep for addEventListener('scroll' combined with getBoundingClientRect(), and for scroll-animation libraries used only for reveals/parallax; check for absence of animation-timeline.
restyleFix: Replace scroll-listener reveals and parallax with animation-timeline: view() / scroll() and animation-range.

title: Combine sticky positioning with scroll timelines
rule: Add scroll timelines over `position: sticky` to create headers that shrink, reading-progress bars, and sidebars that change as the page scrolls.
why: It yields polished scroll-aware chrome without scripting.
doDont: Do: Pair sticky positioning with a scroll timeline for collapsing headers and progress bars. Don't: Update styles from JS scroll handlers on every event.
auditCheck: Check headers and progress bars for JS scroll handlers that set height/width/transform; look for position: sticky paired with animation-timeline.
restyleFix: Make the header sticky and animate its size/progress with animation-timeline: scroll().

title: Size the skeleton from the measured loaded UI
rule: Render the real, loaded component in a browser (Playwright, headless Chrome or any devtools-protocol driver), read each block's box with `getBoundingClientRect()`, and give the skeleton the same sizes and positions instead of eyeballed values.
why: Guessed placeholder sizes make the page jump when real content replaces them (layout jank).
doDont: Do copy measured width, height, gap, radius and line count from the loaded state into the skeleton. Don't pick round-number placeholder heights by feel.
auditCheck: Render the loading and loaded states (or screenshot both) and compare the boxes of corresponding blocks: avatar, title and text lines, media, buttons, and the container's total height. Flag differences of more than a few px or a different number of lines. Grep skeleton components for arbitrary fixed `h-*`/`w-*` values that don't exist in the real component (inference).
restyleFix: Measure the loaded component once, then set skeleton block dimensions, spacing and line count to match; reuse the real component's layout classes or tokens where possible so they cannot drift apart.

title: Prove the skeleton-to-content swap causes no layout shift
rule: After sizing the skeleton, check that replacing it with real content moves nothing: same top and left positions for matching blocks and no change in the surrounding elements' positions (cumulative layout shift near zero).
why: A skeleton that looks right but still shifts content defeats its purpose and hurts perceived stability.
doDont: Do compare element boxes before and after the swap, or record layout-shift entries during load. Don't call the skeleton done because it looks similar.
auditCheck: With a browser tool, capture boxes of the elements below and beside the skeleton in both states, or read `PerformanceObserver` `layout-shift` entries during the swap; media without reserved space (`width`/`height` or `aspect-ratio`) is a likely cause (inference). Text with a different line count than the skeleton is another.
restyleFix: Reserve space for media with `aspect-ratio` or explicit dimensions, set `min-height` on the container for the loaded content, and match line counts; re-measure until the shift is gone.
